hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 초기 해석(덮어쓰기)에 반하는 증거를 제시하고 다음 문장의 출처 혼동 설명으로 연결되므로 B가 옳다. A는 방향 반대, C는 효과의 강도가 아닌 원인 재해석이라는 점에서 배제, D는 실험 참가자와 법정 증인을 혼동하며 지문 내용과도 모순. Loftus & Palmer 실험 묘사는 정확하고 자체 서술이다. 전후 문장 연결이 필요하고 C가 그럴듯한 근접 오답이어서 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Loftus & Palmer(1974)를 바탕으로 한 원작 지문이며, 출처 혼동 해석은 학계 논의와 일치한다. 'however'가 단서가 되지만 C(효과 약화)가 그럴듯한 오답이라 비교 판단이 필요하다. A는 쉽게 배제되고 D는 법정 언급과 연결되어 말이 되는 오답이다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Anthropologist Victor Turner argued that initiation rites do more than announce that a child has become an adult. In his account, initiates pass through a "liminal" phase in which ordinary ranks are suspended: novices are often stripped of names, dressed identically, and made to share hardships. __Out of this leveling, Turner claimed, arises "communitas," an intense sense of equality and solidarity among those undergoing the rite together.__ Researchers studying contemporary adolescent ceremonies have found Turner's framework useful but incomplete. In a study of summer-camp induction rituals, sociologist Mara Delgado observed that campers did report strong bonds during the ritual, yet older counselors deliberately preserved certain hierarchies throughout, suggesting that liminal phases may reshape social structure rather than erase it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Anthropologist Victor Turner argued that initiation rites do more than announce that a child has become an adult. In his account, initiates pass through a "liminal" phase in which ordinary ranks are suspended: novices are often stripped of names, dressed identically, and made to share hardships. __Out of this leveling, Turner claimed, arises "communitas," an intense sense of equality and solidarity among those undergoing the rite together.__ Researchers studying contemporary adolescent ceremonies have found Turner's framework useful but incomplete. In a study of summer-camp induction rituals, sociologist Mara Delgado observed that campers did report strong bonds during the ritual, yet older counselors deliberately preserved certain hierarchies throughout, suggesting that liminal phases may reshape social structure rather than erase it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence from Delgado's study that challenges Turner's account of the liminal phase.
It explains why initiates are stripped of names and dressed identically during initiation rites.
It introduces a criticism of Turner's framework that later researchers have accepted without qualification.
It identifies a consequence Turner attributed to the liminal phase, which a later study partly complicates.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 리미널 단계의 평등화에서 '코뮤니타스'가 생긴다는 Turner의 주장, 즉 그 단계의 결과를 제시하고, 뒤의 Delgado 연구는 유대는 확인하면서도 위계가 유지됨을 보여 이를 부분적으로 복잡하게 만든다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장이 Delgado의 증거가 아니라 Turner의 주장이므로 틀리다. B는 이름 박탈 등은 원인(평등화)으로 앞 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 그 결과를 말할 뿐 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 밑줄 문장이 비판이 아니며, 후속 연구도 '조건 없이' 받아들인 것이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence states Turner's claim that communitas arises from the leveling of the liminal phase, which is a result he attributed to that phase. Delgado's study later confirms the bonds but shows that hierarchies persisted, so it partly complicates the claim, making D correct. A is wrong because the sentence reports Turner's view, not Delgado's evidence. B is wrong because the sentence describes what follows from the stripping of names and identical dress, not why those practices happen. C is wrong because the sentence is not a criticism, and later researchers called the framework incomplete instead of accepting a criticism without qualification.

A(Delgado 증거 아님), B(이유 설명 아님), C(비판 아님·'조건 없이 수용' 아님) 모두 배제 가능. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Turner의 liminality/communitas 개념 서술 정확(Delgado는 가상 연구자로 보이나 사실 오류 아님). 밑줄 문장의 역할을 뒤 문단과 연결해 판단해야 하는 두 단계 구조로 medium에 적합하며, A·C는 후반부 키워드(연구·불완전함)를 차용한 부분적 근거를 가짐.

advisory.note: D가 명확한 정답이다. A(Delgado의 증거로 오인)와 B(원인-결과 혼동)는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 약하지만 말은 된다. 난이도는 medium에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, participants judged which of three comparison lines matched a reference line, a task so easy that people working alone almost never erred. When seated among confederates who unanimously gave a wrong answer, however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical ______ Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence, the wish to avoid standing out from others, rather than to any genuine change in what participants saw.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, participants judged which of three comparison lines matched a reference line, a task so easy that people working alone almost never erred. When seated among confederates who unanimously gave a wrong answer, however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical ______ Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence, the wish to avoid standing out from others, rather than to any genuine change in what participants saw.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: trials,
trials, which
trials;
trials and
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'When seated ... critical trials'는 'participants went along'을 주절로 갖는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'Asch attributed this pattern ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 관계사 which를 넣으면 뒤 절에 이미 목적어 'this pattern'이 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. D는 등위접속사 and 앞에 쉼표가 없어 두 독립절이 제대로 구분되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank is an independent clause whose main verb is "participants went along," and the part after the blank, "Asch attributed this pattern...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own object ("this pattern"), so it can't work as a relative clause. D uses "and" with no comma in front of it, so the two independent clauses aren't properly separated.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 'When seated..., however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical trials'는 종속절+독립절 구조이고, 빈칸 뒤 'Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence...'도 독립절이므로 세미콜론(C)이 유일하게 옳다. A는 comma splice, B는 'which'가 뒤 절에서 문법적 역할이 없어(이미 주어·목적어 완비) 성립 불가, D는 등위접속사 앞 쉼표 누락으로 SAT 관례상 오답(공식 해설 관례 "Without a comma preceding it, 'and' can't be used to join two independent clauses"와 일치). 다만 D는 일반 문법상 가장 논쟁 여지가 있는 오답이지만 SAT 기준에서는 수용 가능. 사실 관계: Asch 1951 실험, 약 1/3(약 32~37%) 동조, 규범적 영향 귀인 모두 타당. 긴 도입구와 삽입된 'however' 때문에 독립절 경계 파악이 필요해 medium에 적합. 저작권 의심 없음(독창적 서술).

advisory.note: 독립절 두 개를 연결하는 표준 문항이다. 빈칸 앞에 도입 종속절이 있고 빈칸 뒤 절은 길어서 훑어 읽으면 틀리기 쉽다. D(쉼표 없는 and)와 B(which)는 그럴듯한 오답이어서 중간 난이도에 맞다. Asch의 연구 내용(약 1/3 동조, 규범적 영향)도 사실과 일치한다.

problem.passage:
Experts and the public often disagree sharply about which hazards deserve the most concern. Psychologist Paul Slovic, who has spent decades asking ordinary people to rank threats such as nuclear power, pesticides, and household chemicals______ that lay estimates of risk are not simply mistaken versions of expert ones. Rather, members of the public weigh qualities such as dread, unfamiliarity, and lack of personal control, factors that technical assessments based on annual fatality counts tend to leave out.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Experts and the public often disagree sharply about which hazards deserve the most concern. Psychologist Paul Slovic, who has spent decades asking ordinary people to rank threats such as nuclear power, pesticides, and household chemicals______ that lay estimates of risk are not simply mistaken versions of expert ones. Rather, members of the public weigh qualities such as dread, unfamiliarity, and lack of personal control, factors that technical assessments based on annual fatality counts tend to leave out.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: argues
, argues,
; argues
, argues
problem.explanation: "who has spent decades ~ chemicals"는 주어 Paul Slovic을 설명하는 비필수 관계절로, 앞에 쉼표가 열려 있으므로 끝에도 쉼표로 닫아야 하고, 그 뒤에 동사 argues가 와야 한다. 그래서 D가 정답이다. A는 관계절을 닫는 쉼표가 없어 argues가 관계절 속 동사처럼 읽힌다. B는 관계절은 제대로 닫지만 동사 argues와 목적어 역할의 that절 사이에 쉼표를 넣어 잘못 끊는다. C는 세미콜론 앞부분이 동사 없는 주어와 수식어뿐이라 독립절이 아니므로 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The clause "who has spent decades ... household chemicals" is a nonessential relative clause describing the subject, Paul Slovic. It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma too, and then the main verb "argues" follows. That makes D correct. A leaves out the closing comma, so "argues" reads as if it belonged to the relative clause. B closes the clause correctly, but it also puts a comma between "argues" and its object, the that-clause, which wrongly splits the verb from what it introduces. C uses a semicolon, but the words before it are only a subject plus a modifier with no main verb, so they aren't an independent clause.

hardJudge.note: D 검산: "Paul Slovic, who has ... chemicals, argues that ..." — 비필수 관계절 쉼표 쌍 닫기 후 본동사. A는 닫는 쉼표 누락, B는 동사-목적어 that절 사이 불필요한 쉼표, C는 세미콜론 앞이 독립절 아님. 모두 명확히 배제됨. 긴 관계절 끝 위치 파악 + 동사-목적어 쉼표 금지 규칙 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합. Slovic의 심리측정 패러다임(dread, unfamiliarity, control) 서술도 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 관계절 앞에 쉼표가 열려 있어 닫는 쉼표가 필요하고, 그 뒤 주절 동사와 that절은 끊으면 안 된다. 그래서 D가 맞다. 관계절이 길어 주절 동사를 놓치기 쉽고, B·A가 그럴듯한 오답으로 작동한다.

problem.passage:
The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, the proposal that the language a person speaks shapes how that person perceives and sorts experience, has often been tested through color vocabulary. Pirahã, a language of the Brazilian Amazon, has been described as having no dedicated basic color words at all, and Hixkaryana, spoken along the Nhamundá River, groups blue and green under a single term______ by contrast, routinely treat the two hues as separate categories.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, the proposal that the language a person speaks shapes how that person perceives and sorts experience, has often been tested through color vocabulary. Pirahã, a language of the Brazilian Amazon, has been described as having no dedicated basic color words at all, and Hixkaryana, spoken along the Nhamundá River, groups blue and green under a single term______ by contrast, routinely treat the two hues as separate categories.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ; English speakers,
, English speakers,
, English speakers
; English speakers
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Pirahã ... single term"은 등위접속된 완전한 절이고, 뒤의 "English speakers ... treat the two hues..."도 독립절이므로 두 절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 한다. 또한 삽입구 "by contrast" 뒤에 쉼표가 있으므로 앞에도 쉼표를 두어 양쪽을 맞춰야 한다. A는 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 삽입구 쉼표는 맞지만 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 comma splice에 삽입구 앞 쉼표까지 빠졌고, D는 세미콜론은 맞지만 "by contrast" 앞 쉼표가 없어 삽입구가 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank ("Pirahã ... under a single term") is a complete independent clause, and so is what follows ("English speakers ... treat the two hues as separate categories"), so you need a semicolon to join them. The interrupting phrase "by contrast" already has a comma after it, so it also needs a comma before it to set it off properly. A does both of these things. B gets the commas around "by contrast" right but joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C has the same comma splice and is also missing the comma before "by contrast," and D uses the correct semicolon but leaves "by contrast" with only one comma, so the interrupting phrase isn't set off correctly.

quality.seed: social science research — Sapir-Whorf linguistic relativity hypothesis and color term categorization across Pirahã Hixkaryana and English-speaking populations

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 "…groups blue and green under a single term"은 독립절, 뒤 "English speakers … treat the two hues as separate categories"도 독립절이므로 세미콜론 필요. "by contrast," 뒤에 쉼표가 이미 있으므로 앞에도 쉼표가 있어야 함 → A가 유일하게 두 조건 충족. B·C는 comma splice, D는 삽입구 쉼표 불균형. 한·영 해설 모두 A를 정확히 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Pirahã 색채어 부재(Everett)와 Hixkaryana의 blue/green 통합은 "has been described as"로 적절히 완화된 서술이며 사실 오류 없음. 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음. 난이도: 세미콜론 판단 + 삽입구 쉼표 짝 맞추기의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B(쉼표 짝 맞음)·D(세미콜론 맞음)가 부분적으로 옳아 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Two decisions are needed: the semicolon between independent clauses and the paired commas around "by contrast". The long compound clause before the blank makes a quick read error-prone. B and D each get one condition right, so they work as attractive distractors.

problem.passage:
In the mountain village of Kuşköy in northeastern Türkiye, farmers have long communicated across steep valleys using kuş dili, or "bird language," a whistled form of Turkish. Researcher Onur Güntürkün found that whistlers do not invent new sounds; instead, they convert the vowels and consonants of spoken Turkish into shifts in pitch and in the timing of whistled notes. A message whistled from one hillside, according to his recordings, can remain intelligible to a listener nearly a kilometer ______ an ordinary shout would fade into the wind long before reaching that distance.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the mountain village of Kuşköy in northeastern Türkiye, farmers have long communicated across steep valleys using kuş dili, or "bird language," a whistled form of Turkish. Researcher Onur Güntürkün found that whistlers do not invent new sounds; instead, they convert the vowels and consonants of spoken Turkish into shifts in pitch and in the timing of whistled notes. A message whistled from one hillside, according to his recordings, can remain intelligible to a listener nearly a kilometer ______ an ordinary shout would fade into the wind long before reaching that distance.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: away, by contrast,
away, whereas,
away, and,
away; by contrast,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A message ... nearly a kilometer away"와 뒤 "an ordinary shout would fade ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 접속부사구 by contrast로 두 독립절을 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론이 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 whereas가 종속접속사라 연결은 가능하지만, 바로 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 접속사와 그 절을 불필요하게 갈라놓는다. C의 and는 등위접속사로 쓸 수 있으나, and 뒤의 쉼표가 접속사와 절을 부당하게 끊고, 의미상 대조도 드러나지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Before the blank you have an independent clause ("A message ... nearly a kilometer away"), and after it you have another one ("an ordinary shout would fade ..."). If you want to join two independent clauses with the transitional phrase "by contrast," you need a semicolon in front of it, so D is correct. A connects the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B's "whereas" is a subordinating conjunction, so it could link the clauses, but the comma right after it wrongly cuts the conjunction off from its clause. C's "and" could also join the clauses, but the comma after it has the same problem, and "and" doesn't express the contrast the sentence needs.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이며 "by contrast"는 접속부사이므로 세미콜론이 필요 → D 정답. A는 콤마 스플라이스, B·C는 접속사(whereas/and) 자체는 가능하나 접속사 뒤 불필요한 쉼표로 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 동일한 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 모순 없음. Kuşköy 휘파람 언어와 Güntürkün 연구는 실제 사실에 부합. 독립절 식별 + 접속부사 vs 접속사 구분이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B·C가 부분적으로 타당한 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞다. 두 독립절 사이에 접속부사 by contrast가 오므로 세미콜론이 필요하다. 오답 B와 C는 접속사 뒤 쉼표 오류로 그럴듯한 함정이다. 사실관계(쿠슈쾨이의 휘파람 언어, 귄튀르퀸의 연구)도 대체로 맞다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In Kalaallisut (West Greenlandic), a single verb can carry information that English spreads across an entire sentence. Linguist Michael Fortescue has documented verbs in which a root is followed by a long chain of suffixes, each one marking tense, mood, or the grammatical roles of the participants ______ one such verb can work as a complete clause, showing on its own who acted on whom.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In Kalaallisut (West Greenlandic), a single verb can carry information that English spreads across an entire sentence. Linguist Michael Fortescue has documented verbs in which a root is followed by a long chain of suffixes, each one marking tense, mood, or the grammatical roles of the participants ______ one such verb can work as a complete clause, showing on its own who acted on whom.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: involved; as a result,
involved, as a result,
involved, as a result;
involved as a result,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Linguist ... involved"와 빈칸 뒤 "one such verb can work as a complete clause..."는 각각 독립절이고, "as a result"는 뒤 절을 앞 절의 결과로 이어 주는 접속부사이다. 따라서 두 절은 세미콜론으로 나누고, 접속부사 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍어야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 두 독립절을 쉼표로만 이은 콤마 스플라이스이다. C는 세미콜론을 "as a result" 뒤에 놓아서, 결과를 나타내는 이 표현이 결과인 뒤 절이 아니라 원인인 앞 절에 붙는다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("Linguist ... involved") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("one such verb can work as a complete clause..."). "As a result" is a transitional phrase that presents the second clause as a consequence of the first. So the two clauses need a semicolon between them, and the transition needs a comma after it, which is why A is correct. B joins two independent clauses with only commas, so it's a comma splice. C puts the semicolon after "as a result," which attaches the phrase to the first clause (the cause) instead of the second clause (the result). D has no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞("Linguist Michael Fortescue has documented verbs ... involved")과 뒤("one such verb can work as a complete clause ...")가 모두 독립절임을 직접 확인함. 접속부사 "as a result"가 뒤 절의 결과 관계를 표시하므로 "; as a result," (A)가 유일하게 올바름. B는 콤마 스플라이스, C는 세미콜론 위치가 접속부사를 앞 절에 붙여 논리 오류, D는 무종지문. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 정확함. Fortescue의 서그린란드어 다종합어 연구 언급은 사실과 부합. 두 절의 독립성 판단 + 접속부사 위치(논리) 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B·C가 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답이어서 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 세미콜론과 접속부사의 위치를 묻는 표준적인 중간 난이도 문항이다. 정답 A가 맞다. 해설 중 D에 대한 설명만 조금 손볼 필요가 있다.

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how the historical origins of the Javanese speech system relate to the way it is used today. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Javanese speakers use Ngoko with close friends and family of equal or lower status, but they use Krama with elders, strangers, and people of higher social rank.

Javanese speech levels took shape in the rigidly ranked royal courts of 16th- to 18th-century Central Java, yet many young urban speakers now reserve Krama for grandparents and use Indonesian in most formal settings.
Javanese, spoken by about 80 million people in Indonesia, has speech levels that developed largely in the royal courts of Central Java between the 16th and 18th centuries.
In 2018, linguist Ika Fitriani found that many young urban Javanese speakers rely on Indonesian, a language without speech levels, in most formal settings.
problem.explanation: 목표는 말씨 체계의 역사적 기원과 오늘날의 사용 방식을 연결하는 것이다. B는 16~18세기 궁정에서 형성된 기원(메모 4)과 젊은 도시 화자의 현재 사용 양상(메모 5)을 대비하며 결합하므로 목표를 달성한다. A는 현재의 사용 규칙만 설명하고 기원은 다루지 않는다. C는 기원만 제시하고 오늘날 사용과의 관계가 없다. D는 현재 경향만 전할 뿐 역사적 기원을 빠뜨렸다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to connect where the speech system came from with how it is used now. B links its origin in the rigidly ranked royal courts of the 16th–18th centuries with today's pattern among young urban speakers, so it does both jobs. A describes only the current rules for using Ngoko and Krama and never mentions the history. C gives only the origin and says nothing about present-day use. D reports only the recent trend and leaves out the historical origins.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 메모 4(궁정 기원)와 메모 5(현재 사용 양상)를 'yet'으로 대비해 결합하여 목표(역사적 기원과 현재 사용의 관계 강조)를 유일하게 충족한다. A·D는 현재 사용만, C는 기원만 다루어 각각 부분적 근거를 가진 오답으로 기능한다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 지지하고 글자 참조가 일치하며 모순이 없다. 영어 해설의 "Your goal"은 학생 관점 표현으로 자연스럽다. 자바어 화자 수(약 8천만), 중부 자바 궁정에서의 말씨 체계 발달 시기는 통념과 부합하며 2018년 연구는 SAT 관행상 허용 가능한 가상 자료다. 두 요소(기원+현재)를 모두 포함하는 선택지를 식별하는 2단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합하다.

advisory.note: 각 오답이 목표의 절반(기원 또는 현재)만 충족하도록 설계되어 비교가 필요하다. 표준 중간 난이도에 맞는다. A는 '현재 사용'으로 볼 여지가 있어 그럴듯하다. 사실관계(약 8천만 화자, 궁정 기원)는 대체로 타당하다. Fitriani 2018 연구는 확인할 수 없으나 문항 내 설정으로 허용된다.

problem.passage:
Among the Mosuo of southwestern China, many adults practice tisese, often translated as "walking marriage": a man visits a female partner at night but returns each morning to the household of his own mother. Children are raised in their mother's matrilineal household, and a child's maternal uncles, rather than the biological father, traditionally share responsibility for the child's upbringing and support. Some earlier anthropologists argued that the nuclear family (a father, a mother, and their children) is a universal unit because cooperation between a child's two biological parents is needed to raise children. Anthropologist Chuan-kang Shih and others counter that the Mosuo case shows children can be raised successfully without that cooperation, as long as they are supported by kin who share a household and its resources.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the counterargument made by Shih and others?
problem.stimulus: Among the Mosuo of southwestern China, many adults practice tisese, often translated as "walking marriage": a man visits a female partner at night but returns each morning to the household of his own mother. Children are raised in their mother's matrilineal household, and a child's maternal uncles, rather than the biological father, traditionally share responsibility for the child's upbringing and support. Some earlier anthropologists argued that the nuclear family (a father, a mother, and their children) is a universal unit because cooperation between a child's two biological parents is needed to raise children. Anthropologist Chuan-kang Shih and others counter that the Mosuo case shows children can be raised successfully without that cooperation, as long as they are supported by kin who share a household and its resources.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the counterargument made by Shih and others?
options: In Mosuo villages, a walking marriage can last for decades, and many fathers know which children they are biologically related to.
In Mosuo villages, households headed by a senior woman tend to own more farmland than households in nearby communities where couples live together.
In Mosuo villages, children's maternal uncles report spending more hours on farm labor than biological fathers in nearby communities do.

In Mosuo villages, children raised in matrilineal households with little contact with their fathers have health and schooling outcomes similar to those of children in nearby communities where couples live together.
problem.explanation: 반론의 핵심은 생물학적 부모의 협력 없이도 같은 가구의 친족 지원만으로 아이가 '성공적으로' 양육될 수 있다는 것이다. D는 아버지와 접촉이 적은 모계 가구 아이들의 건강·학업 결과가 부부 동거 가구 아이들과 비슷하다고 보여 주므로, 양육 성과라는 결과와 부모 협력 부재를 직접 연결해 반론을 지지한다. A는 관계의 지속성과 부성 인지를 말할 뿐 양육 성과와 무관하며, 오히려 부모 연결이 남아 있음을 시사할 수 있다. B는 가구 자원이 많다는 점만 말하고 아이의 양육 결과는 보여 주지 않는다. C는 외삼촌의 노동량을 보여 주지만 노동 시간이 아이가 잘 자란다는 증거가 되지는 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The counterargument says children can be raised successfully without cooperation between their biological parents, as long as kin in the same household support them. D directly supports this: children with little contact with their fathers do about as well in health and schooling as children whose parents live together, which ties the absence of parental cooperation to a successful outcome. A is only about how long relationships last and whether fathers know their children; it says nothing about how the children turn out, and it may even suggest a link between the parents still exists. B shows that the households have plenty of resources but doesn't show any child-rearing outcome. C measures how much uncles work on farms, but hours of labor don't show that the children are being raised successfully.

hardJudge.note: 반론의 핵심 주장("생물학적 부모 협력 없이도 가구 친족 지원만으로 성공적 양육 가능")을 정확히 겨냥한 결과(outcome) 증거는 D뿐임을 직접 검산. Mosuo의 tisese 및 Chuan-kang Shih의 핵가족 보편성 반박은 실제 학술 내용과 부합. 지문은 독창적 요약으로 저작권 우려 없음. 두 단계 판단(반론의 핵심 개념 '성공적 양육' 파악 → 결과 증거와 수단 증거 구별)을 요구해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: D만 성공적 양육 결과와 부모 협력의 부재를 함께 보여 줌. B(가구 자원)와 C(외삼촌의 기여)는 반론의 일부 요소와 겹치므로 비교해야 배제되는 그럴듯한 오답이고, A는 관련은 있지만 결과를 보여 주지 않음. 모쒀족 tisese와 Shih의 논지에 대한 설명도 정확함.

problem.passage:
In a famous 1960s study, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told elementary school teachers that certain students, identified by a test, were about to experience an intellectual "spurt." In fact, these students had been chosen at random. By the end of the year, the selected students showed larger IQ gains than their classmates, especially in the earliest grades. Rosenthal and Jacobson concluded that teachers' raised expectations had caused real improvement in the students' intellectual development. Some critics, however, have proposed a different explanation: the test used to measure IQ was poorly suited to very young children, producing unreliable scores, so the apparent gains may reflect measurement error rather than any genuine change in the students' abilities.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the critics' alternative explanation?
problem.stimulus: In a famous 1960s study, psychologists Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson told elementary school teachers that certain students, identified by a test, were about to experience an intellectual "spurt." In fact, these students had been chosen at random. By the end of the year, the selected students showed larger IQ gains than their classmates, especially in the earliest grades. Rosenthal and Jacobson concluded that teachers' raised expectations had caused real improvement in the students' intellectual development. Some critics, however, have proposed a different explanation: the test used to measure IQ was poorly suited to very young children, producing unreliable scores, so the apparent gains may reflect measurement error rather than any genuine change in the students' abilities.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the critics' alternative explanation?
options: When the selected first and second graders were later assessed by independent examiners using a different, well-validated instrument designed for young children, they again outperformed their classmates by a similar margin.
When the selected first and second graders were later assessed with the original test, several of them received scores that were implausibly high or low for children their age.
When the selected first and second graders were later observed in class, their teachers were found to call on them more often and give them more encouraging feedback than other students.
When the selected first and second graders were later compared with older students in the same school, the older students showed smaller differences between selected and unselected groups.
problem.explanation: 비평가들은 저학년 IQ 점수 상승이 부적합한 검사의 측정 오류 때문이라고 주장한다. A는 신뢰도 높은 다른 도구로 독립적으로 측정해도 같은 격차가 나타났음을 보여 주므로, 결과가 원래 검사의 결함 탓이라는 설명을 직접 약화시킨다. B는 원래 검사 점수가 비현실적이라는 것을 보여 주므로 오히려 비평가들의 설명을 강화한다. C는 교사의 행동 차이를 보여 주어 기대 효과가 일어날 수 있는 경로와 관련은 있지만, 측정된 점수 상승이 실제였는지는 다루지 않는다. D는 저학년에서 효과가 더 컸다는 점을 다시 말할 뿐이며, 이는 어린 아이들에게 검사가 부적합했다는 비평가들의 설명과도 들어맞는다.
problem.explanationEn: The critics say the young students' gains came from measurement error caused by an unsuitable test. Choice A shows that independent examiners using a different, reliable instrument found the same gap, so the result can't simply be blamed on flaws in the original test. That directly weakens the critics' explanation. Choice B shows the original test gave implausible scores, which actually supports the critics. Choice C describes how teachers treated the students differently, which relates to how expectations might work, but it doesn't tell you whether the measured gains were real. Choice D just repeats that the effect was larger in the youngest grades, and that pattern fits the critics' claim about the test being unsuitable for young children too.

quality.seed: social science research — Pygmalion classroom expectancy effect Rosenthal Jacobson teacher predictions and student intellectual development gains measurement

hardJudge.note: 비평가 주장(측정 오류)을 정확히 파악한 뒤 A가 다른 검증된 도구로 동일 격차를 재현해 이를 직접 약화함을 확인해야 함. B는 '검사 점수'를 언급해 훑어 읽으면 고를 수 있는 함정이나 오히려 비평가를 강화하고, C는 기대 효과의 경로와 관련돼 부분적 타당성이 있으며, D는 지문 내용을 재진술해 비평가 설명과 양립함. 로젠탈·제이콥슨 연구 및 검사 신뢰도 비판(Snow, Thorndike)에 대한 서술도 사실과 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 A는 다른 검증된 도구로 독립 측정해도 격차가 재현되었으므로 측정 오류 설명을 직접 약화함. C는 기대 효과 메커니즘을 지지해 매력적인 오답이나 측정 신뢰성 문제를 다루지 않음. B는 비평가 강화, D는 양쪽 설명과 양립. 지문 내용(Rosenthal & Jacobson, 저학년 검사 부적합 비판)은 사실과 부합. 중간 난이도에 적합.

problem.passage:
In a 2019 study of workplace conversations in Osaka, linguist Haruka Ito recorded junior employees declining requests from their supervisors. Rather than refusing outright, the employees typically shifted into keigo, Japanese's honorific register, and left their objections unfinished. One participant explained, "When my manager asks me to stay late, I say only that tonight is a little difficult, and he understands." Ito concluded that such indirectness allowed employees to protect their supervisors' face, preserved the hierarchy that the honorifics signaled, and ______ the refusal itself without ever stating it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a 2019 study of workplace conversations in Osaka, linguist Haruka Ito recorded junior employees declining requests from their supervisors. Rather than refusing outright, the employees typically shifted into keigo, Japanese's honorific register, and left their objections unfinished. One participant explained, "When my manager asks me to stay late, I say only that tonight is a little difficult, and he understands." Ito concluded that such indirectness allowed employees to protect their supervisors' face, preserved the hierarchy that the honorifics signaled, and ______ the refusal itself without ever stating it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: understands
has communicated
communicate
communicated
problem.explanation:
정답 D. 빈칸은 "such indirectness"를 주어로 하는 병렬 동사 "allowed ..., preserved ..., and ______"의 세 번째 항목이다. 앞의 두 동사가 과거형이고, 이를 감싸는 주절 "Ito concluded"도 과거이므로 과거형 communicated가 맞다.
A(understands): 인용문 안의 현재 시제("I say," "he understands")에 맞춘 형태다. 하지만 인용문은 따로 떨어진 발화이고, 빈칸은 과거 시제로 쓰인 Ito의 결론 안에 들어 있다.
B(has communicated): 병렬 항목 중 이것 하나만 현재완료가 되어 allowed, preserved와 형태가 어긋난다.
C(communicate): 바로 앞의 "allowed employees to protect"에 이어지는 원형으로 읽으면 맞는 것처럼 보인다. 그러나 그렇게 읽으면 employees가 communicate의 주어가 되어 의미가 틀어진다. 또 preserved와 함께 이루는 indirectness의 동사 병렬 구조가 깨지고, 단수 주어와 수 일치도 되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
D is correct. The blank is the third verb in a parallel series whose subject is "such indirectness": "allowed ..., preserved ..., and ______." The first two verbs are in the past tense, and the reporting clause "Ito concluded" is also past, so the past-tense "communicated" is required.
A ("understands") copies the present tense used inside the quotation ("I say," "he understands"). But the quotation is a separate statement, and the blank belongs to Ito's past-tense conclusion.
B ("has communicated") makes only one item in the series present perfect, so it no longer matches "allowed" and "preserved."
C ("communicate") seems to work as a bare verb continuing "allowed employees to protect." Read that way, though, it makes the employees the ones communicating, which changes the meaning. It also breaks the parallel series of verbs, including "preserved," that belong to "indirectness," and it doesn't agree with that singular subject.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸은 "such indirectness allowed..., preserved..., and ___"의 세 번째 병렬 동사이며, 주절 "Ito concluded"의 과거 시제와 일치하는 communicated(D)가 유일하게 맞음. A는 직전 인용문의 현재 시제("he understands")에 끌리도록 설계된 함정(체크리스트 3은 '인용문 시제에 이끌린 오답'으로 해석하여 충족 판정), B는 병렬 중 하나만 현재완료, C는 "allowed employees to protect ... and communicate"로 국소적으로 읽히지만 preserved가 그 병렬을 끊고 수 일치도 어긋남. 해설의 각 오답 분석이 정확하고 모순 없음. 인용문과 주절 간 시제 전환을 추적해야 하므로 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함. 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음(가상의 연구).

advisory.note: 세 번째 병렬 동사는 관계절 'that the honorifics signaled'를 건너 추적해야 한다. 인용문의 현재 시제(A)와 바로 앞 to부정사 원형(C)이 유인 오답으로 잘 작동한다. 정답 D는 명확하다.

problem.passage:
In Japanese folklore, tsukumogami are household objects—umbrellas, lanterns, sandals—said to acquire a spirit after roughly a century of use. Folklorist Noriko Reider notes that in medieval picture scrolls, these awakened objects are often shown rampaging only after being discarded during year-end housecleaning, when families threw out old tools to welcome the new year. Some scholars read the tales simply as warnings against wastefulness. Others observe, however, that the scrolls almost never depict well-kept old objects coming to life while still in use; the spirits emerge specifically at the moment an object is cast out, crossing from the orderly household into the space beyond it. If this pattern is meaningful, it suggests that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In Japanese folklore, tsukumogami are household objects—umbrellas, lanterns, sandals—said to acquire a spirit after roughly a century of use. Folklorist Noriko Reider notes that in medieval picture scrolls, these awakened objects are often shown rampaging only after being discarded during year-end housecleaning, when families threw out old tools to welcome the new year. Some scholars read the tales simply as warnings against wastefulness. Others observe, however, that the scrolls almost never depict well-kept old objects coming to life while still in use; the spirits emerge specifically at the moment an object is cast out, crossing from the orderly household into the space beyond it. If this pattern is meaningful, it suggests that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the stories were meant to teach that any object kept for a century would inevitably become dangerous to its owners.
the stories linked the objects' transformation less to age alone than to their passage across the household's boundary.
the stories were meant to discourage families from performing year-end housecleaning altogether.
the stories reflected a belief that newly made objects posed a greater spiritual threat than old ones.
problem.explanation: 지문은 오래 쓰인 물건이라도 계속 사용 중일 때는 거의 깨어나지 않고, 버려져 집 경계 밖으로 넘어가는 순간에 정령이 나타난다고 지적하므로, 변신의 계기가 나이만이 아니라 경계 넘기에 있다는 B가 정답이다. A는 '백 년'이라는 나이 조건을 근거로 삼았지만, 잘 보관된 오래된 물건은 깨어나지 않는다는 관찰과 충돌한다. C는 대청소라는 배경 정보를 활용하지만, 지문의 초점은 버려지는 순간이지 청소 관습 자체를 금지하는 데 있지 않다. D는 새 물건에 대한 언급이 지문에 전혀 없으므로 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage points out that even very old objects almost never come to life while they're still being used. Instead, the spirits appear right when an object is thrown out and crosses from the household into the space beyond it. So the trigger seems to be that boundary crossing, not age alone, which is why B is correct. A builds on the century-of-use detail, but it clashes with the observation that well-kept old objects stay dormant. C picks up on the housecleaning context, but the passage's point is about the moment of discarding, not about stopping the cleaning custom. D has no support, because the passage never mentions new objects at all.

quality.seed: social science research — Tsukumogami Japanese folklore animistic object spirits and liminal transgression boundary crossing temporal possession narratives

hardJudge.note: 지문의 핵심 관찰(사용 중인 오래된 물건은 거의 깨어나지 않음 + 버려지는 순간 정령 출현)을 결합하면 B가 유일하게 논리적으로 완성한다. A는 '백 년' 조건을 과장하여 관찰과 충돌, C는 대청소 배경을 과잉 확장, D는 무근거. 해설(한/영) 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 선택지 참조 정확, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Noriko Reider·연말 대청소 배경 등 사실 관계 문제 없음. 두 정보의 연결이 필요하고 오답 중 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 '오래된 물건도 사용 중에는 깨어나지 않음'과 '버려지는 순간 경계를 넘음'이라는 두 관찰을 이어야 나오는 답이다. A와 C는 지문 속 세부(백 년, 대청소)를 근거로 삼아 그럴듯하게 보이고, D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 레이더(Reider)의 츠쿠모가미 연구 언급은 사실과 대체로 맞다.

problem.passage:
In 1215, a group of rebellious English barons forced King John to accept a document later known as Magna Carta. Many people today picture it as a broad charter of rights for all English people. __In fact, most of its clauses dealt with narrow feudal matters, such as how much money the king could demand from his barons and how inheritances should be handled.__ Even so, the document mattered for a larger reason: it set down in writing the idea that the king himself had to obey the law, a principle that later generations used to limit royal power.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In 1215, a group of rebellious English barons forced King John to accept a document later known as Magna Carta. Many people today picture it as a broad charter of rights for all English people. __In fact, most of its clauses dealt with narrow feudal matters, such as how much money the king could demand from his barons and how inheritances should be handled.__ Even so, the document mattered for a larger reason: it set down in writing the idea that the king himself had to obey the law, a principle that later generations used to limit royal power.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why King John agreed to accept the document that the barons presented to him.
It presents the main claim of the text about why Magna Carta influenced later generations.
It challenges a common belief about Magna Carta by describing what the document mostly contained.
It describes how later generations used Magna Carta to limit the power of English kings.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장 바로 앞에서 많은 사람이 마그나 카르타를 모든 사람을 위한 폭넓은 권리 헌장으로 생각한다고 소개하고, 밑줄 문장은 "In fact"로 시작해 실제로는 대부분 좁은 봉건적 문제를 다뤘다고 말한다. 따라서 흔한 믿음을 반박하는 역할이므로 정답은 C이다. A는 왕이 문서를 받아들인 이유를 말하는데, 밑줄 문장은 이유가 아니라 문서의 내용을 설명한다. B는 글의 핵심 주장인데, 그것은 마지막 문장(왕도 법을 따라야 한다는 원칙)에 있다. D 역시 마지막 문장의 내용이지 밑줄 문장의 내용이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the underlined one says many people picture Magna Carta as a broad charter of rights for everyone. The underlined sentence starts with "In fact" and says most of the clauses actually dealt with narrow feudal matters. So it challenges a common belief, which makes C correct. A is wrong because the sentence describes what the document contained, not why the king accepted it. B is wrong because the text's main claim comes in the last sentence, about the king having to obey the law. D is wrong because the use of the document by later generations is also described in the last sentence, not the underlined one.

quality.seed: history and civics — Magna Carta 1215 feudal rights limitation and royal authority constraint in English constitutional development

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "In fact"로 앞 문장의 통념(모든 영국인을 위한 폭넓은 권리 헌장)을 반박하며 실제 내용(좁은 봉건적 사안)을 제시하므로 C가 정확하다. A(왕이 수용한 이유)는 지문에 없는 내용, B(핵심 주장)와 D(후대의 활용)는 마지막 문장의 내용으로 밑줄 문장과 무관하여 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 지문 다른 부분을 참조해 그럴듯하다. 역사적 사실(1215년, 봉건적 조항 다수, 왕도 법 아래 있다는 원칙)도 정확하다. 담화 표지 하나로 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 한글 혼입 없음. 원문 창작 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: "Many people picture... In fact" 구조라 단서가 바로 보이고 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답 B와 D는 마지막 문장 내용을 끌어온 그럴듯한 함정이다. 역사적 사실도 정확하다(1215년, 봉건적 조항, 법의 지배).

problem.passage:
The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, ended the Thirty Years' War, a conflict that had devastated much of central Europe. Many historians view the treaties as an early foundation of modern international law. They point out that the agreements recognized each ruler's authority over his own territory, so outside powers were expected not to interfere in a state's internal affairs. __The treaties also allowed rulers to choose the official religion of their lands, while protecting some private worship for religious minorities.__ Together, these ideas helped shape a system in which independent states dealt with one another as equals.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, ended the Thirty Years' War, a conflict that had devastated much of central Europe. Many historians view the treaties as an early foundation of modern international law. They point out that the agreements recognized each ruler's authority over his own territory, so outside powers were expected not to interfere in a state's internal affairs. __The treaties also allowed rulers to choose the official religion of their lands, while protecting some private worship for religious minorities.__ Together, these ideas helped shape a system in which independent states dealt with one another as equals.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a criticism that some historians have made about the Peace of Westphalia.
It explains the main reason the Thirty Years' War began in central Europe.
It describes a conflict that continued in Europe after the treaties were signed.
It adds a second feature of the treaties that supports the historians' view.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'also'로 시작해, 앞 문장의 영토 주권 인정에 이어 조약의 또 다른 특징(종교 선택권과 소수 종교 보호)을 덧붙인다. 마지막 문장의 'these ideas'가 두 특징을 함께 묶어 근대 국제법의 토대라는 역사가들의 견해를 뒷받침하므로 정답은 D이다. A는 오답인데, 밑줄 문장은 조약을 비판하지 않고 긍정적인 특징을 서술하기 때문이다. B는 전쟁의 원인이 아니라 조약의 내용을 다루므로 틀렸고, C는 조약 이후에 이어진 갈등이 지문에 전혀 언급되지 않으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "also," which tells you it adds another feature of the treaties (letting rulers choose a religion while protecting some minority worship) to the earlier point about territorial authority. The last sentence then groups "these ideas" together as the basis of the system the historians describe, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence doesn't criticize the treaties; it describes one of their positive features. B is wrong because the sentence is about what the treaties said, not why the war started, and C is wrong because the text never mentions any conflict that continued after the treaties.

quality.seed: history and civics — Treaty of Westphalia 1648 sovereign state system and religious toleration principle establishing modern international law

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'also'로 앞 문장(영토 주권 인정)에 이어 조약의 두 번째 특징(종교 선택권·소수 종교 사적 예배 보호)을 덧붙이고, 마지막 문장의 'these ideas'가 이를 역사가들의 견해 뒷받침으로 묶으므로 D가 정답임을 직접 확인함. 역사적 사실(1648년 체결, 30년 전쟁 종결, 통치자의 종교 결정권과 소수 종교 사적 예배 보호, 베스트팔렌 주권 개념을 '많은 역사가'로 한정 서술)도 정확함. 오답 A(비판), B(전쟁 원인—종교가 실제 전쟁 원인이었으므로 그럴듯한 함정), C(이후 갈등)는 전형적 오개념으로 적절하며 터무니없지 않음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 같은 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'also' 신호어 하나로 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: 역사적 사실(cuius regio 원칙 확인, 소수 종교의 사적 예배 보호)은 정확함. 'also'라는 단서가 직접 드러나 easy 수준에 맞음. 오답 B·C는 다소 쉽게 배제되지만 전쟁/갈등이라는 지문 소재를 활용해 그럴듯함.

problem.passage:
In 1868, a group of reformers restored formal power to Japan's emperor and began building a strong central government in Tokyo. Within a few years, the new leaders ended the special privileges of the samurai ______ former warriors could no longer wear swords in public or collect payments from the state.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In 1868, a group of reformers restored formal power to Japan's emperor and began building a strong central government in Tokyo. Within a few years, the new leaders ended the special privileges of the samurai ______ former warriors could no longer wear swords in public or collect payments from the state.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: class,
class
class;
class, and,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the new leaders ended ... the samurai class"와 빈칸 뒤 "former warriors could no longer ... state"는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 융합문이다. D는 등위접속사 and 뒤에 쉼표를 찍어 접속사와 그 뒤 절 사이를 불필요하게 끊으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank ("the new leaders ended ... the samurai class") and the part after it ("former warriors could no longer ... the state") are both independent clauses, since each has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between them, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds a comma after the conjunction "and," which wrongly separates "and" from the clause that follows it.

problem.stimulus: Convened by German chancellor Otto von Bismarck in November 1884, the Berlin Conference brought together representatives of fourteen states, none of them African, to settle competing claims along the Congo and Niger Rivers. Among the conference's most consequential outcomes, the principle of "effective occupation," which required a power to demonstrate actual administrative control over a coastal territory before other signatories would recognize its claim, ______ European states to rush officials, soldiers, and treaties into the African interior in the years that followed.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: having pushed
pushing
were pushing
pushed
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "the principle"이고, 쉼표 사이의 which절은 삽입된 수식어이므로 빈칸에는 주절의 정동사가 필요하다. D의 "pushed"는 단수 주어와 일치하는 과거 시제 정동사이므로 정답이다. A의 "having pushed"와 B의 "pushing"은 분사여서 정동사 역할을 할 수 없기 때문에 주절이 완성되지 않는다. C의 "were pushing"은 정동사이지만 복수형이어서, 바로 앞의 "outcomes"나 "signatories"를 주어로 잘못 본 경우에 고르게 되는 오답이다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "the principle," and the which-clause set off by commas is just an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs the main verb of the sentence. Choice D, "pushed," is a finite past-tense verb that agrees with a singular subject, so it is correct. Choices A ("having pushed") and B ("pushing") are participles, which can't work as a main verb, so the sentence would be left without one. Choice C, "were pushing," is a finite verb, but it's plural. You'd pick it only if you mistook the nearby plural nouns "outcomes" or "signatories" for the subject.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "the principle"(단수) + 삽입 which절 뒤 주절 정동사 필요 → "pushed"만 적합. A·B는 비정동사, C는 복수형(인접 복수 명사 "outcomes"/"signatories"에 의한 근접 오류 유도). 한·영 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 베를린 회의(1884년 11월, 비스마르크 소집, 14개국, 아프리카 국가 불참, 실효적 점령 원칙) 사실 관계 정확. 삽입절을 건너 주어를 찾고 정동사 여부를 판단하는 두 단계 추론으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 the principle과 빈칸 사이에 긴 which절이 끼어 있어 정동사 여부와 수 일치를 함께 판단해야 하므로 두 단계 판단에 해당한다. C는 바로 앞의 복수 명사(signatories, outcomes)에 이끌려 고르기 쉬운 유인 오답이다. 역사적 사실(1884년 11월 소집, 14개국 참가, 아프리카 국가 불참, 실효적 점유 원칙의 해안 지역 적용)에도 오류가 없다.

problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "provisions," and the clause "which ... naturalization" is an interruption that sits between the subject and its verb. That means the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, so A is correct. B is a finite verb, but it's singular—it matches nearby singular nouns like "path" or "country" instead of the real subject. C and D are participles, so they would leave the sentence without a main verb, and it wouldn't be a complete sentence.

problem.passage:
When Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, it did not free a single enslaved person in the border states loyal to the Union, nor in Confederate areas already under federal control. It applied only to territory still in rebellion, where the Union had no immediate power to enforce it. Critics at the time mocked the document for declaring freedom precisely where it could not be granted. Yet the proclamation's limited reach was deliberate: Lincoln justified it as a war measure under his authority as commander in chief, an authority that extended only to enemy territory. Framed this way, the order turned every advance of Union troops into an advance of emancipation and opened the Union army to Black enlistment, eventually adding nearly 180,000 soldiers. A document that seemed to accomplish little on the day it was signed thus reshaped what the war was being fought to achieve.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options: Although critics mocked the Emancipation Proclamation, it immediately freed most enslaved people living in the Confederacy.
Although the Emancipation Proclamation's scope was narrow, that narrowness reflected its legal basis and allowed it to transform the Union war effort.
Although the Emancipation Proclamation applied to Confederate territory, its main purpose was to keep the border states loyal to the Union.
Although the Emancipation Proclamation added soldiers to the Union army, Lincoln regretted limiting it to areas in rebellion.
problem.explanation: 지문은 선언의 적용 범위가 좁았다는 비판을 소개한 뒤, 그 한계가 최고사령관 권한이라는 법적 근거에서 의도된 것이며 결과적으로 북군의 진격을 해방과 연결하고 흑인 입대를 열어 전쟁의 목적을 바꾸었다고 말한다. B가 이 두 단계를 모두 담는다. A는 선언이 즉시 노예를 해방했다고 하여 집행력이 없었다는 지문과 모순된다. C는 접경주가 언급되긴 하지만 충성 유지를 주목적으로 서술한 근거가 없다. D는 입대 증가는 맞지만 링컨이 후회했다는 내용은 지문에 없고, 오히려 한계는 의도적이었다.
problem.explanationEn: The text first notes the criticism that the proclamation's reach was limited, then explains that this limit was deliberate because it rested on Lincoln's war powers, and finally shows that it linked Union advances to emancipation and opened enlistment to Black soldiers. Choice B captures both steps. Choice A contradicts the text, which says the Union could not enforce the order where it applied. Choice C mentions the border states, but the text never says keeping them loyal was the main purpose. Choice D is right about the added soldiers, but the text never says Lincoln regretted the limit; it says the limit was intentional.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검산 완료: 지문은 '좁은 범위 → 법적 근거로 의도됨 → 전쟁 수행 변화'의 구조이며 B가 이를 정확히 요약. problem.passage:
In 1903, Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU) in Manchester, frustrated that decades of petitions and polite lobbying had failed to win British women the vote. The group soon adopted the motto "Deeds, not words," interrupting political meetings, staging mass marches, and, after 1912, smashing shop windows and setting fire to empty buildings. Historians have long debated whether such tactics advanced or delayed suffrage. Historian June Purvis argues that the escalation was less a burst of anger than a calculated response to government stonewalling: each time Parliament shelved a suffrage bill, the WSPU raised the stakes in order to keep the issue in newspaper headlines that ministers could not ignore. Critics at the time, by contrast, claimed that the window-breaking alienated sympathetic lawmakers. Purvis acknowledges this cost but maintains that the suffrage question had stayed politically alive largely because of the attention militancy generated.

According to the text, how does Purvis interpret the WSPU's increasingly aggressive actions?

problem.question: According to the text, how does Purvis interpret the WSPU's increasingly aggressive actions?
options: As an emotional reaction to decades of failed petitions that ultimately cost the movement the support of sympathetic lawmakers
As a tactic copied from earlier reform campaigns that had used petitions and polite lobbying to pressure Parliament
As a deliberate strategy, intensified after each legislative setback, to keep public and political attention on the vote
As a short-lived experiment that the WSPU abandoned once newspapers began criticizing its destruction of property
problem.explanation: Purvis는 과격화를 분노의 폭발이 아니라 정부가 법안을 보류할 때마다 수위를 높여 언론 주목을 유지하려는 계산된 대응으로 보므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Purvis가 부정한 '감정적 반응'을 내세우고 비판자들의 주장을 섞었다. B는 청원과 로비가 실패했기 때문에 전술을 바꿨다는 지문 내용과 반대로, 그 방식을 모방했다고 한다. D는 전술을 포기했다는 언급이 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct because Purvis sees the escalation as a "calculated response" to stonewalling by the government: every time Parliament shelved a suffrage bill, the WSPU raised the stakes to stay in the headlines. A describes the escalation as an emotional reaction, which Purvis specifically rejects, and it mixes in what the critics claimed. B says the WSPU copied petition-based methods, but the passage says the WSPU turned to militancy because those methods had failed. D claims the WSPU dropped the tactics, and the passage never says that.

advisory.note: A는 지문 내용(청원 실패, 비판자의 주장, Purvis의 인정)을 섞어 놓아 그럴듯한 오답이다. B는 "petitions and polite lobbying"이라는 지문 표현을 다시 써서 잘못 연결하게 만든다. problem.passage:
After seizing power in October 1917, the Bolsheviks promised to build a society organized according to Marxist principles, in which workers rather than owners would control factories. In the first months, many factory committees did take over management, and party leaders initially praised these efforts as proof that the revolution was reaching ordinary people. By 1918, however, output had collapsed amid civil war and shortages, and Lenin began insisting that plants be run by single appointed managers, often former owners or engineers, answerable to central state agencies. Historians note that this shift did not mean the Bolsheviks abandoned their ideology; rather, leaders reinterpreted Marxism to argue that a strong centralized state was a necessary stage before workers could govern directly. The result was that the practical meaning of "workers' control" changed sharply within a year of the revolution.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanationEn: D is correct. The text explains that the crisis moved factory management away from workers' committees and toward appointed managers, and that leaders justified this by reinterpreting Marxism instead of abandoning it. problem.passage:
In March 1918, Soviet Russia signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany and its allies, formally leaving the First World War. The terms were severe: Russia gave up control over Poland, the Baltic territories, Finland, and Ukraine, regions that together held roughly a third of its population and much of its industry and farmland. Many historians have described the treaty as a humiliating surrender forced on a collapsing state. Yet Vladimir Lenin, who pushed the agreement through over fierce objections from within his own party, saw it differently. He argued that the new Bolshevik government could not survive if it kept fighting a war its exhausted army had already stopped waging. In his view, giving up territory was a temporary price for gaining the breathing space needed to secure power at home. Events partly supported this reasoning: when Germany was defeated later that year, the treaty was annulled, and the Bolsheviks, still in control, moved to reclaim several of the lost regions.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options: Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk imposed heavy losses on Russia, Lenin accepted it as a short-term sacrifice to preserve the Bolshevik government, a judgment later events partly bore out.
Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was opposed within the Bolshevik party, Lenin's support for it was driven mainly by his confidence that Germany would soon lose the war.
Although the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk ended Russia's role in the war, its loss of farmland and industry caused the Bolshevik government's eventual collapse.

problem.explanationEn: The text first lays out the treaty's harsh territorial losses, then explains that Lenin saw them as a temporary price for keeping the Bolsheviks in power, and finally notes that later events partly supported his view. That is why A is correct. B gets the opposition within the party right, but the text says Lenin acted because the army was exhausted and he needed to secure power at home, not because he predicted Germany's defeat. C correctly mentions the lost farmland and industry, but the text says the Bolsheviks stayed in control, which is the opposite of a collapse. D contradicts the text's description of the terms as severe, and the text never says what Russia's leaders expected.

problem.passage:
By 1923, Germany's inability to meet its war reparations payments had brought French and Belgian troops into the Ruhr and pushed the German mark into hyperinflation. The plan drafted in 1924 by a committee chaired by American banker Charles Dawes did not reduce the total amount Germany owed. Instead, it lowered the annual payments for the first several years, tied later installments to the country's economic recovery, reorganized the German central bank, and arranged a large loan, much of it raised from American investors. Historians note that the plan's apparent success rested on a fragile foundation: Germany used borrowed American money to pay France and Britain, which in turn used those funds to repay their own war debts to the United States. When American lending dried up after 1929, the cycle collapsed, and the stability the plan had seemed to produce disappeared along with it.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The Dawes Plan ended the occupation of the Ruhr by significantly reducing the total reparations Germany was required to pay.
The Dawes Plan restored European stability mainly by reorganizing Germany's central bank, a reform that protected the German economy after 1929.
The Dawes Plan eased Germany's reparations burden for a time, but the stability it brought depended on a continuing flow of American loans.
The Dawes Plan failed immediately because American investors refused to lend money to Germany while its currency suffered from hyperinflation.
problem.explanation: 이 글은 도스 플랜이 초기 연간 지불액을 줄여 부담을 덜어 주었다는 점과, 그로 인한 안정이 미국 차관의 순환에 의존해 1929년 이후 무너졌다는 점을 함께 서술하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 루르 점령이라는 배경을 언급하지만, 지문은 계획이 총 배상액을 줄이지 않았다고 명시하므로 틀렸다. B는 중앙은행 개편이라는 실제 세부 사항을 쓰지만, 그것을 안정의 주된 원인으로 보고 1929년 이후에도 경제를 지켰다고 주장해 지문의 붕괴 서술과 모순된다. D는 미국 대출을 언급하지만, 지문에서 미국 투자자들은 실제로 대출을 해 주었고 계획은 한동안 성공한 것처럼 보였으므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct because the text makes two connected points: the Dawes Plan lowered Germany's early annual payments, and the stability that followed depended on a cycle of American lending that fell apart after 1929. A brings up the real background of the Ruhr occupation, but the text says outright that the plan did not reduce the total amount Germany owed. B uses a real detail, the reorganization of the central bank, but it treats that change as the main source of stability and says it protected the economy after 1929, which contradicts the text's account of the collapse. D mentions American loans, but in the text American investors did lend money, and the plan appeared to succeed for several years.

problem.passage:
Many popular accounts credit Mohandas Gandhi's campaigns of nonviolent resistance, such as the 1930 Salt March, with single-handedly ending British rule in India in 1947. Historians generally agree that these campaigns eroded the moral legitimacy of colonial rule, both in India and abroad. ______ many scholars also point to factors Gandhi did not control: the financial strain Britain suffered during the Second World War, the 1946 mutiny of sailors in the Royal Indian Navy, and growing doubts in London about whether the empire could still be governed at all.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Many popular accounts credit Mohandas Gandhi's campaigns of nonviolent resistance, such as the 1930 Salt March, with single-handedly ending British rule in India in 1947. Historians generally agree that these campaigns eroded the moral legitimacy of colonial rule, both in India and abroad. ______ many scholars also point to factors Gandhi did not control: the financial strain Britain suffered during the Second World War, the 1946 mutiny of sailors in the Royal Indian Navy, and growing doubts in London about whether the empire could still be governed at all.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Consequently,
For example,
In other words,
Even so,
problem.explanation: 정답은 D이다. 앞 문장은 간디의 운동이 식민 통치의 정당성을 약화했다고 인정하고, 뒤 문장은 간디가 통제하지 못한 다른 요인들을 제시한다. 그래서 '단독으로 끝냈다'는 통념에 단서를 다는 양보 후 반전 관계가 된다. A는 정당성 약화가 전쟁 비용이나 해군 반란을 낳은 것처럼 인과 관계를 만드는데, 지문은 이 요인들을 간디와 무관하다고 밝힌다. B는 뒤 문장이 앞 문장의 사례인 것처럼 연결하지만, 뒤 문장의 요인들은 도덕적 정당성 약화의 예가 아니다. C는 같은 내용을 다르게 말하는 관계인데, 뒤 문장은 새로운 요인을 더하는 대조적 내용이다.
problem.explanationEn: D is correct. The previous sentence admits that Gandhi's campaigns weakened the legitimacy of colonial rule. The next sentence lists factors outside his control, which pushes back on the claim that he ended British rule "single-handedly." That is a concession followed by a qualification. A suggests the campaigns caused the war costs and the mutiny, but the passage says Gandhi did not control these factors. B treats the next sentence as an example of the previous one, but those factors are not examples of moral delegitimization. C signals a restatement, but the next sentence adds new and contrasting information.

advisory.note: 양보 후 반전 관계(Even so)가 명확하다. 'single-handedly' 통념과 뒤 문장의 외부 요인을 연결해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. Consequently와 For example은 그럴듯한 오답이다. 역사적 사실(1930 소금 행진, 1946 인도 해군 반란, 1947 독립)에 오류가 없다.

problem.passage:
Between 1378 and 1417, Latin Christendom was divided by rival claimants to the papacy, first two and eventually three, each with cardinals, courts, and royal supporters of his own. Many historians have treated the Great Schism as a pure catastrophe that drained the Church's moral authority and opened the way for later reformers. __Yet the crisis also forced theologians and canon lawyers to ask a question that had long seemed unthinkable: whether a general council of the Church might hold authority even over a pope.__ Writers such as Jean Gerson argued that it could, and the Council of Constance (1414–1418) put that argument into practice by deposing or accepting the resignation of all three claimants and electing Martin V. For this reason, some scholars now see the Schism not only as a breakdown but also as the source of a lasting debate about where legitimate authority in an institution ultimately lies.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

For this reason, some scholars now see the Schism not only as a breakdown but also as the source of a lasting debate about where legitimate authority in an institution ultimately lies.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It names a reformer whose later criticism of the Church is said to have grown directly out of the damage the Schism caused.
It gives evidence that backs up the claim that the Schism mainly weakened the Church's moral standing.
It brings in a consequence of the Schism that complicates the view just mentioned and leads into the text's example of a council.
It explains how the rival claimants tried to justify their separate claims to the papacy in front of royal supporters.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 분열을 순전한 재앙으로만 보는 앞 문장의 시각과 대비되는 결과(공의회가 교황보다 위에 있을 수 있는가라는 물음)를 제시하고, 이어지는 Gerson과 콘스탄츠 공의회 사례로 연결되므로 C가 정답이다. A는 '후대 개혁가'가 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 특정 개혁가를 언급하지 않으며, Gerson은 비판자가 아니라 공의회 권위를 옹호한 인물이다. B는 밑줄 문장이 그 견해를 뒷받침하는 것이 아니라 오히려 복잡하게 만든다는 점에서 틀렸다. problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet," so it pushes back against the view that the Schism was a pure catastrophe. It does this by pointing to another result: scholars began asking whether a council could hold authority over a pope. That question leads straight into the examples of Gerson and the Council of Constance, so C is correct. A is wrong because later reformers are mentioned in the sentence before, but the underlined sentence names no reformer, and Gerson defended a council's authority rather than criticizing the Church. B is wrong because the sentence complicates the catastrophe view instead of supporting it. D is wrong because the rival claimants and their royal supporters do appear in the text, but the underlined sentence is about questions raised by theologians and canon lawyers, not about how the claimants justified themselves.
