hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞의 '순전한 재앙' 시각과 대비되는 결과(공의회 권위 문제)를 도입하고 이어지는 Gerson·콘스탄츠 공의회 사례로 이어지므로 C가 정확함. A(개혁가 미언급), B(견해를 뒷받침이 아니라 복잡화), D(교황 측 정당화가 아닌 신학자들의 물음)는 모두 지문 요소를 부분 차용한 매력적 오답. 역사적 사실(1378–1417 분열, 세 명의 교황 주장자, Gerson의 공의회주의, 콘스탄츠 공의회 1414–1418의 폐위/사임 수용 및 Martin V 선출) 모두 정확. 영어 해설에서 'scholars began asking'은 지문의 'theologians and canon lawyers'를 다소 느슨하게 지칭하나 결론·글자 참조는 한국어 해설과 일치하고 한글 없음. 'Yet' 신호가 비교적 명확하지만 대비 파악과 뒤 사례 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 사실관계(1378–1417, 콘스탄츠 공의회 1414–1418, Gerson, 마르티노 5세)는 정확함. 오답 A·B·D는 지문 요소를 부분적으로 차용해 그럴듯함. 'Yet'이 단서로 강해 다소 쉬운 편이지만 medium 범위 내.

problem.passage:
The Hundred Years' War (1337–1453) is often presented as a simple contest between two nations, England and France, fighting over territory. Historian Anne Curry and others have pointed out, however, that the conflict began as a feudal succession dispute: Edward III of England claimed the French crown through his mother, while the French nobility backed Philip VI, a cousin descended through the male line. __Because many of the lords who fought were tied to both crowns by land and oath, a knight in Gascony or Brittany could reasonably see himself as defending a rightful lord rather than a homeland.__ For this reason, these historians argue, the national loyalties that later chroniclers projected onto the war's early decades mostly took shape as the fighting went on, rather than causing it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: The Hundred Years' War (1337–1453) is often presented as a simple contest between two nations, England and France, fighting over territory. Historian Anne Curry and others have pointed out, however, that the conflict began as a feudal succession dispute: Edward III of England claimed the French crown through his mother, while the French nobility backed Philip VI, a cousin descended through the male line. __Because many of the lords who fought were tied to both crowns by land and oath, a knight in Gascony or Brittany could reasonably see himself as defending a rightful lord rather than a homeland.__ For this reason, these historians argue, the national loyalties that later chroniclers projected onto the war's early decades mostly took shape as the fighting went on, rather than causing it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces the territorial claims that the text goes on to describe as the war's main cause.
It raises a challenge to the historians' view that the conflict began as a succession dispute.
It describes the specific regions where the war's earliest battles were fought.
It shows how the war's feudal origins shaped participants' allegiances, supporting the text's final claim.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장에서 말한 봉건적 계승 분쟁이라는 기원이 실제 참전자들의 충성 대상(조국이 아닌 정당한 영주)에 어떤 영향을 주었는지 보여 주고, 마지막 문장의 '민족적 충성은 전쟁 중에 형성되었다'는 결론을 뒷받침하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 영토가 언급되지만 글은 영토를 주된 원인으로 보지 않으므로 틀리다. B는 밑줄 문장이 역사가들의 견해에 반박하는 것이 아니라 오히려 지지하므로 틀리다. C는 가스코뉴와 브르타뉴가 언급되지만 전투 장소를 설명하려는 것이 아니라 충성 관계를 보여 주는 예시이므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence shows how the war's origin as a feudal succession dispute affected the people who fought: they were loyal to a rightful lord, not a homeland. That point supports the final sentence's claim that national loyalties developed during the war, so D is correct. A is wrong because the text mentions land but doesn't treat territory as the main cause. In fact, the text argues against that view. B is wrong because the sentence supports the historians' view instead of challenging it. C is wrong because Gascony and Brittany are mentioned to show divided loyalties, not to identify where the first battles took place.

quality.seed: history and civics — Hundred Years War 1337-1453 English French territorial conflict and feudal succession dispute resolution

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장(봉건적 계승 분쟁)과 마지막 문장(민족적 충성은 전쟁 중 형성)을 연결하는 근거 역할을 하므로 D가 명확히 옳다. A는 '영토'라는 글의 도입부 표현을, C는 '가스코뉴·브르타뉴'라는 지명을 각각 부분 근거로 삼아 훑어 읽으면 끌릴 수 있고, B는 '그러나'의 흐름을 오독한 구조적 오답으로 말이 된다. 역사적 사실(에드워드 3세의 모계 계승 주장, 필리프 6세의 남계 사촌, 앤 커리의 연구)도 정확하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조도 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 원문은 창작 문단으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 오답 A·C는 지문 속 표면 단서(영토, 지명)를 이용한 함정이고 B는 기능을 반대로 읽은 오답이다. 정답 D는 앞 문장과 뒤 문장을 이어서 읽어야 고를 수 있으므로 medium 난이도에 맞는다. 'For this reason'이 단서가 되어 다소 쉬워질 여지는 있다.

problem.passage:
Between 1405 and 1433, the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven fleets across the Indian Ocean, reaching ports from Java to the Swahili coast. Many popular accounts describe these voyages as missions of discovery, comparable to later European expeditions. __Yet the routes Zheng He followed had been sailed by Arab, Persian, and Gujarati merchants for centuries, and his pilots relied on charts and navigational knowledge already circulating in those trading networks.__ Historian Geoff Wade and others therefore argue that the fleets are better understood as instruments of the Ming tributary system: by displaying overwhelming naval power and distributing lavish gifts, the court persuaded distant rulers to send envoys acknowledging the emperor's supremacy.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Between 1405 and 1433, the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven fleets across the Indian Ocean, reaching ports from Java to the Swahili coast. Many popular accounts describe these voyages as missions of discovery, comparable to later European expeditions. __Yet the routes Zheng He followed had been sailed by Arab, Persian, and Gujarati merchants for centuries, and his pilots relied on charts and navigational knowledge already circulating in those trading networks.__ Historian Geoff Wade and others therefore argue that the fleets are better understood as instruments of the Ming tributary system: by displaying overwhelming naval power and distributing lavish gifts, the court persuaded distant rulers to send envoys acknowledging the emperor's supremacy.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a fact that undermines a common characterization of the voyages, setting up an alternative interpretation of their purpose.
It presents a fact that explains how the Ming court was able to persuade distant rulers to send envoys acknowledging the emperor.
It presents a fact that supports the comparison between Zheng He's voyages and later European expeditions described earlier.
It presents a fact that illustrates the extensive reach of the fleets across ports from Java to the Swahili coast.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해, 항로가 이미 수 세기 동안 알려져 있었다는 사실을 제시하며 항해를 '발견'의 임무로 보는 대중적 시각을 약화시킨다. 이어서 'therefore'로 조공 체제의 도구라는 대안적 해석이 제시되므로 A가 정답이다. B는 마지막 문장의 설득 방식(해군력과 선물)과 연결되지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 방법을 설명하지 않는다. C는 유럽 탐험과의 비교를 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 비교를 지지하는 것이 아니라 반박한다. D는 첫 문장의 항해 범위와 관련 있어 보이지만, 밑줄 문장의 초점은 항로가 새롭지 않았다는 점이다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and points out that the routes had been sailed for centuries. That fact weakens the popular view of the voyages as missions of discovery, and the next sentence ("therefore") offers another reading: the fleets were tools of the tributary system. So A is correct. B ties into the final sentence about persuading rulers, but the underlined sentence never explains how persuasion worked; that sentence names naval power and gifts instead. C mentions the comparison to European expeditions, but the underlined sentence argues against that comparison rather than supporting it. D picks up on the fleets' reach, but the underlined sentence is about the routes already being known, not about how far the fleets went.

quality.seed: history and civics — Zheng He treasure voyages 1405-1433 Ming Dynasty maritime exploration and tributary system expansion Indian Ocean

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 '발견의 임무'라는 대중적 특성화를 반박하고, 다음 문장의 'therefore'가 조공 체제라는 대안적 해석으로 이어지므로 A가 정확히 기능을 기술한다. B(설득 방식 설명), C(비교 지지), D(범위 예시)는 각각 지문의 다른 문장과 연결되어 부분적 그럴듯함을 가지나 밑줄 문장의 실제 역할과 불일치한다. 역사적 사실(1405–1433, 7차 항해, Geoff Wade의 조공·무력 투사 해석) 문제 없음. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 'Yet'과 'therefore' 두 담화 표지를 연결해야 하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 'Yet'에서 'therefore'로 이어지는 흐름 때문에 정답 A를 찾기가 비교적 쉽다. 오답 C는 지문 내용과 정반대여서 빨리 배제된다. 그래도 B(마지막 문장의 설득 방식)와 D(첫 문장의 항해 범위)는 지문 속 정보와 부분적으로 연결되므로 비교가 필요하다. 그래서 medium 수준의 하단으로 판단한다. Geoff Wade가 원정을 조공 체제·해양 원시 식민주의 관점에서 해석했다는 서술은 대체로 맞다.

problem.passage:
Historians often describe the Columbian Exchange, the transfer of plants, animals, and pathogens between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia after 1492, as a story of loss for the Americas, where smallpox and measles killed a large share of Indigenous peoples. Historian Rebecca Earle complicates this picture by noting that some American crops changed population patterns far beyond the Atlantic world. __Maize and potatoes, for instance, grew well in soils and climates where wheat and rice failed, and by the eighteenth century they were supporting rapid population growth in places as distant as northern Europe and highland China.__ Earle argues, therefore, that the Exchange should be understood not only as a demographic catastrophe in one hemisphere but also as a demographic engine in others.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Historians often describe the Columbian Exchange, the transfer of plants, animals, and pathogens between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia after 1492, as a story of loss for the Americas, where smallpox and measles killed a large share of Indigenous peoples. Historian Rebecca Earle complicates this picture by noting that some American crops changed population patterns far beyond the Atlantic world. __Maize and potatoes, for instance, grew well in soils and climates where wheat and rice failed, and by the eighteenth century they were supporting rapid population growth in places as distant as northern Europe and highland China.__ Earle argues, therefore, that the Exchange should be understood not only as a demographic catastrophe in one hemisphere but also as a demographic engine in others.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the deaths caused by smallpox and measles in the Americas were smaller than historians commonly assume.
It explains why Earle believes that wheat and rice were less important to world history than the crops introduced from the Americas.
It offers examples supporting the claim that American crops reshaped populations in regions far from where they originated.
It describes a consequence of the Columbian Exchange that Earle regards as more significant than its effects in the Americas.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 바로 앞 문장의 주장, 즉 일부 아메리카 작물이 대서양 세계 너머의 인구 양상을 바꾸었다는 주장을 옥수수·감자의 구체적 사례로 뒷받침하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 질병 피해를 축소하는 근거로 읽었지만, 지문은 피해를 부정하지 않고 다른 측면을 덧붙일 뿐이다. B는 밀과 쌀이 언급되긴 하나, 그 작물들의 역사적 중요도를 비교하는 것이 문장의 목적은 아니다. D는 마지막 문장의 '~뿐 아니라 ~도'를 놓친 것으로, Earle는 두 효과를 함께 인정할 뿐 어느 쪽이 더 중요하다고 순위를 매기지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct because the underlined sentence gives concrete examples, maize and potatoes, to back up the sentence right before it: some American crops changed populations far beyond the Atlantic world. A is wrong because the text never says the death toll from disease was overestimated. It adds another side to the story without denying the losses. B is wrong because wheat and rice show up only to explain where the American crops did well. The sentence isn't ranking them by historical importance. D misses the "not only... but also" in the last sentence: Earle accepts both effects and never says one matters more than the other.

quality.seed: history and civics — Columbian Exchange 1492 onward plants animals diseases transfer and demographic consequences Americas Europe

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 직전 문장의 주장(아메리카 작물이 대서양 세계 너머의 인구 양상을 바꿈)을 옥수수·감자라는 구체 사례로 뒷받침하므로 C가 정확함. A는 질병 사망 규모 축소 주장이 지문에 없고, B는 밀·쌀이 단지 아메리카 작물의 적응력을 보여주는 배경으로만 언급되며, D는 'not only... but also' 구조상 Earle가 우열을 매기지 않으므로 배제됨. D와 B가 부분적 근거를 가진 매력적 오답으로 기능하여 medium 난이도에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설이 동일한 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. Rebecca Earle은 실존 역사가(감자·식량사 연구)로 내용과 모순되지 않으며, 옥수수·감자의 유럽·중국 인구 성장 기여도 역사학적 통설과 일치.

advisory.note: 정답 C 명확. D는 마지막 문장의 'not only...but also'를 확인해야 배제되고, B는 밀·쌀 언급으로 부분 근거가 있어 medium 난이도에 적합. 사실관계도 문제없음(Earle, Feeding the People 등 관련 연구).

problem.passage:
In his 1944 book Capitalism and Slavery, historian Eric Williams, a Trinidadian scholar who later led his country to independence, argued that profits from the triangular trade—in which ships carried manufactured goods to West Africa, enslaved people to the Caribbean, and sugar back to Britain—helped finance British industrialization ______ later economic historians have questioned whether those profits were large enough to have played such a decisive role.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In his 1944 book Capitalism and Slavery, historian Eric Williams, a Trinidadian scholar who later led his country to independence, argued that profits from the triangular trade—in which ships carried manufactured goods to West Africa, enslaved people to the Caribbean, and sugar back to Britain—helped finance British industrialization ______ later economic historians have questioned whether those profits were large enough to have played such a decisive role.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , however, later
however, later
; however later
; however, later
problem.explanation: 긴 동격구와 대시 삽입구를 걷어 내면 'Williams argued that ... helped finance British industrialization'과 'later economic historians have questioned ...'라는 독립절 두 개가 남는다. 두 독립절 사이에 접속부사 however가 오면 앞에는 세미콜론, 뒤에는 쉼표를 두어야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 however 뒤 쉼표는 맞지만 앞이 쉼표뿐이라 comma splice가 된다. B는 두 절을 아무 부호 없이 이어 run-on이 된다. C는 세미콜론으로 절 경계는 맞게 표시했지만 접속부사 however 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다.
problem.explanationEn: If you strip away the long appositive and the dash interruption, you're left with two independent clauses: "Williams argued that ... helped finance British industrialization" and "later economic historians have questioned ...". When the conjunctive adverb "however" joins two independent clauses, it takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so D is correct. A puts the right comma after "however," but it has only a comma before it, which makes a comma splice. B runs the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on. C marks the boundary between the clauses correctly with a semicolon but leaves out the comma that has to follow "however."

quality.seed: history and civics — Triangular trade transatlantic slavery system and merchant capitalism colonial commerce networks

hardJudge.note: 두 독립절(Williams argued that... / later economic historians have questioned...) 사이 접속부사 however → '; however,' 필요. D 정답 검산 완료. A는 comma splice, B는 run-on, C는 however 뒤 쉼표 누락으로 각각 배제되며 A·C는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교가 필요. 긴 동격구·대시 삽입구로 절 경계 식별 단계가 추가되어 medium에 적합. 역사적 사실(1944년 저서, 트리니다드 독립 지도) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: Williams(1944) 및 이후 반론(Anstey, Engerman 등) 관련 사실은 정확하다. 긴 삽입 요소 때문에 절 경계를 찾는 데 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, A와 C는 각각 부분적으로 맞아 비교해야만 배제된다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Historians of economics often note that Adam Smith's 1759 treatise The Theory of Moral Sentiments, a book that rooted ethics in the human capacity for sympathy and drew heavily on Smith's long conversations with his friend David Hume______ was overshadowed for generations by his later and more famous study of commerce, The Wealth of Nations.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Historians of economics often note that Adam Smith's 1759 treatise The Theory of Moral Sentiments, a book that rooted ethics in the human capacity for sympathy and drew heavily on Smith's long conversations with his friend David Hume______ was overshadowed for generations by his later and more famous study of commerce, The Wealth of Nations.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , was
; was
was
— was
problem.explanation: "a book that ... David Hume"는 주어 The Theory of Moral Sentiments를 설명하는 비필수 동격어구로, 쉼표로 시작했으므로 쉼표로 닫아야 하며 그 뒤에 동사 was가 이어진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론으로 주어와 동사 was를 갈라놓아 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이 아니게 된다. C는 동격어구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어 어디까지가 삽입인지 불분명해진다. D의 대시는 삽입을 닫는 기능은 있지만, 쉼표로 열었던 삽입을 대시로 닫으면 짝이 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a book that ... David Hume" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, The Theory of Moral Sentiments. Because it opens with a comma, it has to close with a comma before the verb "was," so A is correct. B puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, and neither side of it is an independent clause. C leaves the appositive with nothing closing it, so you can't tell where the interruption ends. D uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but a dash can't close one that opened with a comma, because the punctuation has to match.

quality.seed: history and civics — Scottish Enlightenment eighteenth century intellectual movement and economic philosophy David Hume Adam Smith

hardJudge.note: 검산: 주어 "The Theory of Moral Sentiments" 뒤에 쉼표로 시작한 비필수 동격구("a book that ... David Hume")가 삽입되었고, 동사 "was overshadowed"가 이어지므로 쉼표로 닫는 A가 유일하게 올바르다. problem.passage:
In the months following the Declaration of Independence in July 1776, several newly independent states drafted constitutions to replace their colonial charters. Pennsylvania's constitution, adopted that September by a convention meeting in Philadelphia, was among the most radical of these early frameworks ______ abolished the office of governor entirely, placing lawmaking power in a single-chamber assembly whose members faced election every year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the months following the Declaration of Independence in July 1776, several newly independent states drafted constitutions to replace their colonial charters. Pennsylvania's constitution, adopted that September by a convention meeting in Philadelphia, was among the most radical of these early frameworks ______ abolished the office of governor entirely, placing lawmaking power in a single-chamber assembly whose members faced election every year.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , it
; it
it
and it
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Pennsylvania's constitution ... was among the most radical of these early frameworks"는 삽입구가 있지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "it abolished ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and가 있어 그럴듯해 보이지만 두 독립절을 잇는 and 앞에 쉼표가 빠져 있어 표준 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Even with its long interrupting phrase, the part before the blank ("Pennsylvania's constitution ... was among the most radical of these early frameworks") is a complete independent clause, and "it abolished ..." after the blank is another one. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D looks reasonable because it has the conjunction "and," but when "and" joins two independent clauses, it needs a comma before it, and D leaves that comma out.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞(삽입구 포함 독립절)과 뒤("it abolished...") 모두 독립절이므로 세미콜론(B)이 정답. A는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 독립절을 잇는 and 앞에 쉼표가 없어 SAT 규약상 오답. 다만 D의 '쉼표 없는 and'는 일부 문체 지침에서 허용되는 회색 지대라 가장 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능하며, 긴 삽입구가 절 경계 파악을 요구해 medium에 부합. 역사적 사실(1776년 9월 필라델피아 채택, 주지사직 폐지, 단원제, 연례 선거) 정확. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 1776년 펜실베이니아 헌법(9월, 필라델피아 회의)이 주지사직을 없애고 단원제 의회와 매년 선거를 둔 것은 사실과 맞다. 행정권은 최고행정위원회가 맡았다. 정답은 세미콜론(B) 하나로 정해진다. 빈칸 앞 삽입구가 첫 절이 완전한 절인지 판단하기 어렵게 만들고, D(쉼표 없는 and)가 비교해 봐야 배제되는 오답이어서 medium 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.passage:
When Haiti enacted its Civil Code in 1825, legislators borrowed much of its structure from France's Napoleonic Code of 1804, the legal framework of the very empire that had tried to restore slavery on the island only two decades earlier______ Haitian jurists adapted key provisions to the needs of a nation founded by formerly enslaved people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: When Haiti enacted its Civil Code in 1825, legislators borrowed much of its structure from France's Napoleonic Code of 1804, the legal framework of the very empire that had tried to restore slavery on the island only two decades earlier______ Haitian jurists adapted key provisions to the needs of a nation founded by formerly enslaved people.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , however
; however
; however,
, however,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 긴 동격구("the legal framework of ... earlier")로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "Haitian jurists adapted ..."도 독립절이다. 접속부사 however로 두 독립절을 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표를 써야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 무종지문(comma splice)이 되며, D는 however 양쪽 쉼표가 삽입구처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만 여전히 틀리다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 문장 첫머리 접속부사 however 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank is an independent clause that ends with a long appositive ("the legal framework of ... earlier"), and "Haitian jurists adapted ..." after the blank is also an independent clause. To join two independent clauses with the conjunctive adverb "however," you put a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so C is correct. A and D link the two clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. D can look right because the commas around "however" make it read like an aside, but it's still a splice. B gets the semicolon right but leaves out the comma that has to follow "however" when it opens a clause.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞은 도입 종속절+주절+긴 동격구로 이루어진 독립절, 뒤는 독립절. 접속부사 however로 연결 시 "; however," 필요 → C 정답 확인. A·D는 comma splice, B는 however 뒤 쉼표 누락(SAT 관례상 오답). 긴 동격구가 독립절 경계를 가려 정독이 필요하고 D가 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 하므로 medium 적합. 역사적 사실(1825 아이티 민법전, 1804 나폴레옹 법전, 1802 노예제 복원 시도) 문제없음. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치.

advisory.note: Napoleon's attempt to restore slavery dates to 1802–1803, about two decades before 1825, so the historical claim holds. The long appositive hides where the clause boundary is, which makes this a good medium-level item. One caveat: the Haitian Civil Code is usually dated 1825–1826, but that is within an acceptable range.

problem.passage:
John Snow, a young surgeon's apprentice who treated stricken coal miners when cholera swept through northern England in 1831 and 1832, came to doubt the popular belief that the disease was carried by foul-smelling air ______ 1849, he published an essay arguing that cholera spread through water contaminated with the waste of infected people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: John Snow, a young surgeon's apprentice who treated stricken coal miners when cholera swept through northern England in 1831 and 1832, came to doubt the popular belief that the disease was carried by foul-smelling air ______ 1849, he published an essay arguing that cholera spread through water contaminated with the waste of infected people.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , in
in
, which in
; in
problem.explanation: 긴 동격 삽입구(a young surgeon's apprentice ... 1832)를 건너뛰면 주절은 "John Snow ... came to doubt the popular belief ... air"이고, 빈칸 뒤 "in 1849, he published ..."도 주어 he가 있는 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 되고, B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 관계사 which를 넣지만 뒤 절에 이미 주어 he가 있어 which가 문장 안에서 할 역할이 없으므로 비문이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: If you skip over the long appositive (a young surgeon's apprentice ... 1832), the main clause is "John Snow ... came to doubt the popular belief ... air," and what follows the blank, "in 1849, he published ...," is also an independent clause with its own subject, he. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so D is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice, and B puts them together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds the relative pronoun which, but the clause after it already has a subject (he), so which has no job to do in the sentence and the result is ungrammatical.

A는 comma splice, B는 run-on(단 "air in 1849"로 읽히는 함정이 있어 오답으로서 그럴듯함), C는 which가 뒤 절에서 문법적 역할이 없어 비문. 사실관계(1831–32 킬링워스 탄광 콜레라 진료, 1849년 수인성 전파 논문)도 정확. 긴 동격 삽입구를 건너뛰어 주절 구조를 파악해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 동일 결론과 선택지 참조, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 긴 동격 삽입구를 건너뛰고 주절을 찾은 뒤 독립절 두 개의 연결 방식을 판단해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요합니다. B와 C는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하게 보입니다. Snow의 1831~32년 킬링워스 광부 치료와 1849년 에세이 출판은 사실과 일치합니다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , which by 1853,
problem.explanation: 긴 동격구(a failed ... Jesus)를 걷어내면 주절은 'Hong Xiuquan ... founded the God Worshipping Society ... in the 1840s'이고, 빈칸 뒤 'his followers had captured ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 정답은 A이다. B는 'by 1853' 뒤 쉼표는 맞지만 두 절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 which가 관계절을 만드는 듯 보이지만 관계절 안에 his followers라는 주어가 따로 있고 which가 맡을 역할이 없어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: If you set aside the long appositive (a failed ... Jesus), the main clause is "Hong Xiuquan ... founded the God Worshipping Society ... in the 1840s," and the words after the blank, "his followers had captured ...," form another independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so A is correct. B puts a comma correctly after "by 1853," but joining two clauses with only a comma creates a comma splice. C joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D looks like it starts a relative clause, but that clause already has its own subject, "his followers," so "which" has no job to do and the sentence doesn't work.

Signed in 1842 aboard a British warship anchored on the Yangtze River, the Treaty of Nanjing—the first of what Chinese historians would later call the "unequal treaties" ______ the Qing government to open five coastal cities, including Shanghai and Guangzhou, to British merchants and to cede the island of Hong Kong.

problem.stimulus: Signed in 1842 aboard a British warship anchored on the Yangtze River, the Treaty of Nanjing—the first of what Chinese historians would later call the "unequal treaties" ______ the Qing government to open five coastal cities, including Shanghai and Guangzhou, to British merchants and to cede the island of Hong Kong.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , forced
—forced
; forced
forced
problem.explanation: "the first of ... 'unequal treaties'"는 주어 the Treaty of Nanjing을 설명하는 동격 삽입구로, 앞에서 대시로 열렸으므로 같은 대시로 닫아야 하고 그 뒤에 동사 forced가 와야 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표를 써서 삽입구를 닫으려 하지만 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫으면 문장부호가 짝이 맞지 않는다. C의 세미콜론은 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 동사 없는 불완전한 문장이 된다. D는 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입구가 끝나는 지점이 표시되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "the first of ... 'unequal treaties'" is an appositive that describes the subject, the Treaty of Nanjing. It opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too, and then the verb "forced" follows. That makes B correct. A tries to close the appositive with a comma, but a phrase opened with a dash can't be closed with a comma because the punctuation doesn't match. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, which leaves the first part as an incomplete sentence with no verb. D has no closing punctuation at all, so nothing shows where the appositive ends.

hardJudge.note: 대시로 연 동격 삽입구를 대시로 닫는 짝맞춤 문제. 주어(the Treaty of Nanjing)와 동사(forced) 사이의 삽입구 경계를 파악하고 여는 부호와 일치시키는 두 단계 판단이 필요. A(쉼표로 동격 닫기)와 D(부호 생략)는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯한 오답이며 C도 문장부호로서 말이 됨. 역사적 사실(1842년, 양쯔강 정박 HMS Cornwallis, 5개 항구 개항, 홍콩 섬 할양, 최초의 불평등 조약) 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 대시 짝 맞추기 문항으로 표준적이다. 앞부분에 쉼표가 있는 분사구가 있어 A가 그럴듯해 보이는 함정이 된다. 역사적 사실(1842년, HMS Cornwallis, 5개 항구, 홍콩 할양)은 정확하다.

- The Tanzimat ("reorganization") was a period of reform in the Ottoman Empire lasting from 1839 to 1876.

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how far the reforms of 1856 extended beyond those of 1839. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Tanzimat began with the 1839 Edict of Gülhane and ended in 1876, when reformers helped bring about the empire's first constitution.
Like the 1850 commercial code, which was modeled on French law, the 1856 Reform Edict reflected the Tanzimat's interest in European legal systems.
Whereas the 1839 Edict of Gülhane had promised all subjects security of life and property, the 1856 Reform Edict declared Muslims and non-Muslims equal before the law.
The 1839 Edict of Gülhane promised fair taxation, and the 1876 constitution, though suspended two years later, created an elected parliament.
problem.explanation: 목표는 1856년 개혁이 1839년 개혁보다 얼마나 더 나아갔는지 강조하는 것이다. C는 1839년 칙령의 생명·재산 보장과 1856년 칙령의 종교 간 법적 평등을 대조해 확장된 범위를 보여 준다. A는 탄지마트의 시작과 끝을 말할 뿐 1856년 칙령을 언급하지 않는다. B는 1856년 칙령을 다루지만 1850년 상법과의 공통점을 말할 뿐 1839년과 비교하지 않는다. D는 1839년과 1876년을 연결해 1856년이 빠져 있다.

problem.passage:
Wheat growers who sell their harvest on the spot market face prices that can swing sharply within a single season. To limit this exposure, many farmers lock in a sale price months before harvest by selling futures contracts. The practice of hedging a portion of expected output with such contracts, according to agricultural economists who have tracked farm incomes across several decades, ______ year-to-year revenue considerably, though it also caps the gains farmers can capture when spot prices surge.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The practice of hedging a portion of expected output with such contracts, according to agricultural economists who have tracked farm incomes across several decades, ______ year-to-year revenue considerably, though it also caps the gains farmers can capture when spot prices surge.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: stabilize
stabilizes
stabilizing
have stabilized
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The practice'이며, 'of hedging ... contracts'와 'according to ... decades'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 단수 주어에 맞는 정동사가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사(contracts, economists, decades)에 맞춘 복수형이어서 주어와 수가 일치하지 않는다. C는 분사라서 문장에 정동사가 없게 되어 완전한 문장이 되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The practice." The phrases "of hedging ... contracts" and "according to ... decades" are just modifiers that come between the subject and its verb. So the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject, which makes B correct. A and D are finite verbs, but they're plural forms that match the nearby plural nouns (contracts, economists, decades) instead of the actual subject. C is a participle, so it would leave the sentence without a main verb, and it wouldn't be a complete sentence.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'The practice'(단수)와 동사 사이에 'of hedging ... contracts', 'according to ... decades' 두 개의 긴 삽입구가 있어 주어 식별 + 수 일치라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A·D는 인접 복수 명사에 이끌릴 수 있는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 정동사 부재로 배제된다. 정답 B 검산 완료. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 자연스럽다. 선물 헤징이 수익을 안정시키되 상승 이익을 제한한다는 내용도 사실에 부합한다.

advisory.note: 주어(The practice)와 동사 사이에 수식어구가 두 개 끼어 있어 근처 복수 명사에 끌리기 쉬운 구조라서 medium 난이도에 맞음. A와 D가 복수 함정, C가 비정동사 오답으로 잘 구성됨.

problem.passage:
In the late nineteenth century, many American petroleum refiners began acquiring the pipelines, storage tanks, and crude-oil fields that supplied their plants. Economists have often explained this backward integration as a bid for market power: a firm that owned its suppliers could squeeze out rivals. Economic historian Lena Marsh argues that this account misses a more ordinary motive. Refiners that bought crude on the open market had to bargain repeatedly with independent producers and pipeline operators, and they often faced sudden price demands when supplies ran short. Writing and enforcing contracts to guard against such behavior was costly and frequently failed. By owning the supply chain, Marsh contends, refiners replaced these uncertain negotiations with internal coordination, lowering the everyday expense of keeping their refineries running. Monopoly ambitions, in her view, were sometimes present but were not what made integration attractive to most firms.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Writing and enforcing contracts to guard against such behavior was costly and frequently failed. problem.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 Marsh가 후방 통합을 시장 지배력 때문이 아니라, 외부 공급자와 반복 협상하고 계약을 집행하는 데 드는 비용을 내부 조정으로 줄이려는 일상적 동기로 설명한다는 것이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 Marsh가 반박하는 기존 경제학자들의 설명(경쟁자 축출)이다. B는 계약이 비용이 많이 들고 자주 실패했다는 내용을 '불법'으로 왜곡했다. D는 공급 부족이라는 세부 사항을 빌려 왔지만, 정제보다 유전 소유가 더 큰 이익을 냈다는 주장은 지문에 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's central point is that Marsh explains backward integration not by market power but by an ordinary motive: owning suppliers swapped costly, repeated bargaining and unreliable contracts for internal coordination. That makes C correct. A gives the market-power explanation that Marsh is arguing against. B distorts the text, which says contracts were costly and often failed, not that they were illegal. D borrows the detail about supply shortages, but the text never claims that owning fields was more profitable than refining.

problem.passage:
Economists have long assumed that a shopper's willingness to pay for a product reflects a stable, internal sense of its value. Studies of anchoring complicate that assumption. In one experiment, participants first wrote down the last two digits of an arbitrary number and then bid on items such as wireless keyboards and bottles of wine. Those whose digits were high consistently bid more than those whose digits were low, even though everyone understood that the number had nothing to do with the products.

Researchers who followed up on this finding noticed something further. Once an anchor had set a buyer's initial valuation, later price changes were judged relative to that starting point rather than in absolute terms. A buyer anchored high tended to treat a moderate price increase as tolerable, while a buyer anchored low reacted to the same increase by sharply cutting the quantity purchased. The anchor, in other words, shaped not only how much people were willing to pay at first but also how sensitive their demand was to subsequent changes in price.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
problem.stimulus:
Economists have long assumed that a shopper's willingness to pay for a product reflects a stable, internal sense of its value. Studies of anchoring complicate that assumption. In one experiment, participants first wrote down the last two digits of an arbitrary number and then bid on items such as wireless keyboards and bottles of wine. Those whose digits were high consistently bid more than those whose digits were low, even though everyone understood that the number had nothing to do with the products.

Researchers who followed up on this finding noticed something further. Once an anchor had set a buyer's initial valuation, later price changes were judged relative to that starting point rather than in absolute terms. A buyer anchored high tended to treat a moderate price increase as tolerable, while a buyer anchored low reacted to the same increase by sharply cutting the quantity purchased. The anchor, in other words, shaped not only how much people were willing to pay at first but also how sensitive their demand was to subsequent changes in price.
problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Arbitrary numbers influence what buyers will pay for inexpensive goods but have little effect on their bids for costly items such as wine.
Buyers who receive a high anchor will pay more at first, but their demand eventually becomes more sensitive to price than that of buyers given a low anchor.
Economists have abandoned the view that willingness to pay reflects internal value, since buyers no longer judge price changes in absolute terms.
An irrelevant reference point can affect both a buyer's starting valuation of a product and how strongly that buyer responds when the price later changes.
problem.explanation: 지문은 첫 단락에서 무관한 숫자(앵커)가 초기 입찰가에 영향을 준다고 하고, 둘째 단락에서 그 앵커가 이후 가격 변화에 대한 수요 민감도까지 좌우한다고 말한다. D는 이 두 가지를 모두 담고 있으므로 정답이다. A는 저가품과 고가품을 구분하지만, 지문에서 와인도 영향을 받았으므로 틀렸다. B는 높은 앵커가 초기 지불액을 높인다는 점은 맞지만, 오히려 높은 앵커를 받은 구매자가 가격 인상에 덜 민감했으므로 민감도 비교를 거꾸로 서술했다. C는 지문이 기존 가정을 '복잡하게 만든다'고만 했을 뿐 경제학자들이 이를 버렸다고 하지 않았고, 단정적 표현도 지나치다.
problem.explanationEn: The first paragraph shows that an arbitrary number (an anchor) affects buyers' initial bids, and the second shows that the same anchor also shapes how sensitive their demand is to later price changes. D captures both points, so it is correct. A splits cheap goods from expensive ones, but the text says bids on wine were affected too. B is right that a high anchor raises the initial amount buyers will pay, but it reverses the sensitivity comparison: buyers anchored high were actually less responsive to a price increase. C overstates the text, which says anchoring studies "complicate" the old assumption, not that economists have abandoned it.

hardJudge.note: D correctly synthesizes both paragraphs (anchor affects initial valuation + price sensitivity). A contradicted by wine example; B reverses the sensitivity relationship (high anchor = less sensitive); C overstates "complicate" as "abandoned." Korean and English explanations align with each other and with the choices. Two-paragraph synthesis with two partially-correct distractors (B, C) suits medium. advisory.note: 두 단락의 내용을 함께 종합해야 풀린다. B는 앞부분은 맞고 비교 방향만 거꾸로 되어 있고, C는 과장된 진술이며, A는 지문에 없는 구분을 끌어들인다. Ariely 앵커링 실험을 각색했지만 지문은 새로 쓴 글이다.

problem.passage:
Economists have long assumed that when a cement producer charges distant customers more than nearby ones, the gap simply reflects the added cost of trucking heavy loads over longer distances. Studying delivered prices across several regional markets, economist Lena Okafor found a more complicated pattern. Customers located near a rival plant often paid less than the extra trucking cost would predict, while customers with no nearby alternative supplier paid noticeably more than that cost alone could explain. Okafor concluded that producers set delivered prices partly according to how much competition each location faces, so a buyer's distance from the plant explains only part of the price that buyer pays.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Studying delivered prices across several regional markets, economist Lena Okafor found a more complicated pattern. Okafor concluded that producers set delivered prices partly according to how much competition each location faces, so a buyer's distance from the plant explains only part of the price that buyer pays.

Then Okafor finds that buyers near rival plants pay less, while buyers with no alternative supplier pay more, so prices also depend on competition. That makes A the answer. B only restates the old assumption that the text calls incomplete. C overgeneralizes by saying prices drop for every customer, when only buyers near rivals pay less. D offers advice that the text never gives.

problem.passage:
Many companies pay their sales representatives through tournament-style schemes, in which bonuses depend not on how much each person sells but on how each person ranks against colleagues. Economists have long argued that such schemes sharpen effort, since a modest gain in sales can lift a worker past a rival and into a much larger prize. Yet a 2021 field study of a regional insurance firm by economist Laila Haddad complicates this view. When the firm widened the gap between first- and second-place bonuses, top-ranked and bottom-ranked agents changed little, while agents in the middle of the rankings sharply increased the number of client calls they made. Haddad concluded that steeper prizes do raise effort, but mostly among workers who believe a single strong month could realistically change their position; those far ahead or far behind see little reason to respond.

Based on the text, what did Haddad's study suggest about the firm's agents?
problem.stimulus: Many companies pay their sales representatives through tournament-style schemes, in which bonuses depend not on how much each person sells but on how each person ranks against colleagues. Economists have long argued that such schemes sharpen effort, since a modest gain in sales can lift a worker past a rival and into a much larger prize. Yet a 2021 field study of a regional insurance firm by economist Laila Haddad complicates this view. When the firm widened the gap between first- and second-place bonuses, top-ranked and bottom-ranked agents changed little, while agents in the middle of the rankings sharply increased the number of client calls they made. Haddad concluded that steeper prizes do raise effort, but mostly among workers who believe a single strong month could realistically change their position; those far ahead or far behind see little reason to respond.
problem.question: Based on the text, what did Haddad's study suggest about the firm's agents?
options: Larger differences between bonus levels raised effort fairly evenly across all agents, confirming the long-standing argument of economists.
Larger differences between bonus levels mattered chiefly to agents whose rank seemed open to change in the near term.
Larger differences between bonus levels discouraged bottom-ranked agents so much that their client calls declined below earlier levels.
Larger differences between bonus levels mattered chiefly to top-ranked agents, who worked harder to protect their first-place prizes.
problem.explanation: 지문에 따르면 상금 격차를 키웠을 때 순위 중간에 있는 직원들만 고객 전화를 크게 늘렸습니다. Haddad는 그 이유를 이들이 한 달만 잘해도 순위를 바꿀 수 있다고 믿기 때문이라고 결론지었으므로 B가 정답입니다. A는 노력이 높아졌다는 부분은 맞지만, 노력이 고르게 늘었다고 말해 상위와 하위 직원의 변화가 적었다는 내용과 모순됩니다. C는 하위 직원이 반응하지 않았다는 부분은 맞지만, 전화 수가 줄었다는 내용은 지문에 없습니다. D는 실제로 거의 변화가 없었던 상위 직원에게 효과를 돌리고 있으므로 오답입니다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says that when the bonus gap grew, only the agents in the middle of the rankings made many more client calls. Haddad explained this by saying these agents believed one strong month could change their rank, so B is correct. A gets it right that effort rose, but it says the rise was even across all agents, which contradicts the text's point that top and bottom agents changed little. C is right that bottom agents didn't respond, but the text never says their calls dropped. D gives the effect to top-ranked agents, who actually changed little, so it is wrong.

hardJudge.note: 지문의 결과(중간 순위 직원만 전화 급증)와 Haddad의 결론(한 달로 순위를 바꿀 수 있다고 믿는 직원)을 연결하면 B가 명확히 도출됨. A는 '노력 증가'는 맞지만 '고르게'가 상위·하위 변화 미미와 모순, C는 '하위 미반응'은 맞지만 '감소'는 근거 없음, D는 상위 직원 귀속으로 지문과 상반. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 글자 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 가상 연구로 사실 오류·저작권 문제 없음. 두 정보 연결이 필요한 medium 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 지문의 '중간 순위' 내용을 '순위가 바뀔 수 있어 보이는 직원'으로 바꿔 말한 것으로, 표현 전환과 결론을 연결해야 풀 수 있다. A, C, D는 각각 일부만 맞는 근거를 가지고 있다.

problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives a specific finding: plants with spare parts and spare lines handled shortages well. The sentence after the blank restates what that finding means in general terms, saying that "wasteful" slack actually works as a buffer. So D is correct. A may look tempting because the passage contrasts the lean view with the research, but the two sentences around the blank point the same way and don't contradict each other. B would introduce an example, but the final sentence is a generalization, not an example. C would add a parallel case, but the final sentence sums up the earlier point instead of adding a new one.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 문장(구체적 연구 결과)과 뒤 문장(그 의미의 일반화·재진술) 관계상 D 'In other words'가 가장 논리적임. A는 지문 전반의 대비 구조 때문에 유인력이 있고, B·C는 각각 예시·유사 사례 추가 기능으로 배제 가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 모순 없음. 지문은 창작 내용으로 저작권 의심 없음. 두 문장의 관계를 정독해야 하고 A가 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞의 연구 결과를 일반화해 다시 말한 것이므로 D가 성립한다. 지문 첫머리의 린 생산 관점과 대비되는 흐름 때문에 A가 그럴듯한 오답이 되고, B와 C는 사례를 덧붙이는 기능인지 요약하는 기능인지를 구분해야 배제된다. 다만 'Thus'도 어느 정도 말이 되지만 선택지에는 없다.

problem.passage:
Retailers that sell seasonal goods, such as winter coats or patio furniture, face a recurring dilemma: when to cut prices on unsold stock. Traditionally, many chains marked items down on a fixed calendar, applying discounts to all stores in the same week. Analysts at several apparel companies have argued that this approach ignores local variation in demand, since a cold spell in one region can keep coats selling at full price while stores elsewhere are already overstocked. __Yet when one chain tested store-by-store markdown timing based on weekly sales forecasts, it found that the forecasts were reliable only in stores with several years of sales history, while newer locations saw no improvement over the fixed calendar.__ The result suggests that flexible markdown timing may be most useful where enough past data exist to predict how local demand will change over a season.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

It reports a finding that limits how widely the analysts' proposed alternative can be expected to succeed.

A는 반박의 방향은 일부 맞지만, 기존 매장에서는 개선이 있었으므로 비판을 '완전히 뒤집는' 것은 아니다. C는 한파 사례가 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 사례를 보여주는 문장이 아니다. D는 고정 달력과 비교한 내용이 있어 그럴듯하지만, 소매업체들이 처음 그 방식을 채택한 이유는 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence starts with "Yet" and reports that store-by-store markdown timing helped only in stores with long sales histories, so it limits how widely the analysts' proposed alternative can be expected to work. The final sentence backs this up by concluding that flexible timing works best where there is enough data, so B is correct. A gets the direction partly right, but the test did not fully overturn the criticism, because established stores did improve. C refers back to the cold-spell example in the previous sentence, but the underlined sentence does not illustrate that example. D sounds plausible because the sentence compares results to the fixed calendar, but it never explains why retailers adopted that calendar in the first place.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 분석가들의 대안(매장별 할인 시점)에 대한 실험 결과를 제시하며, 판매 이력이 긴 매장에서만 효과가 있었다는 점에서 대안의 적용 범위를 제한한다. 마지막 문장이 이를 뒷받침하므로 B가 정확하다. A는 '완전히 뒤집는다'가 과장(기존 매장에서는 개선 있음), C는 앞 문장의 사례를 가리킬 뿐, D는 고정 달력 채택 이유를 다루지 않음. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 지지하고 글자 참조도 선택지와 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'Yet' 전환 파악 + 마지막 문장과의 연결이라는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 A·D가 부분적 근거를 가진 오답으로 기능하여 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B는 'Yet'으로 시작하는 한정 기능과 마지막 문장의 결론에 들어맞는다. A는 'fully'라는 극단적 표현 때문에, C는 앞 문장과 혼동시키는 선택지라서, D는 채택 이유가 지문에 없어서 배제된다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Economists have long puzzled over why some shoppers seem to prefer a handbag or watch precisely because it costs more. One explanation draws on the problem of asymmetric information: a seller knows far more about a product's materials and craftsmanship than a buyer can learn in a store. When quality is hard to verify, a high price can act as a signal, since only a firm confident that its goods will satisfy customers can afford to charge a premium and still earn repeat business. __Yet a price alone is cheap to set, and a new firm could simply copy a luxury label's price tag without matching its stitching or leather.__ What makes the signal credible, researchers argue, is the brand reputation built over decades: a firm with a long record has much to lose if a single disappointing product damages trust, so its premium price is backed by that accumulated reputation in a way a newcomer's price is not.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Economists have long puzzled over why some shoppers seem to prefer a handbag or watch precisely because it costs more. It describes a strategy commonly used by new firms, illustrating how premium pricing helps unfamiliar brands enter luxury markets.
It raises a weakness in the explanation just described, setting up the claim about what allows a high price to convey quality reliably.

problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "가격만으로 신호가 된다"는 앞의 설명에 대해, 가격은 누구나 흉내 낼 수 있다는 한계를 지적한다. 이어지는 문장은 그 한계를 브랜드 평판으로 해결하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 한계를 지적한 것은 맞지만 지문은 신호 이론을 버리지 않고 보완한다. B는 신생 기업이 언급되지만 그것은 가설적 모방 사례일 뿐 시장 진입에 도움이 된다는 내용이 아니다. D는 정보 비대칭과 관련은 있으나 밑줄 문장은 문제를 재진술하는 것이 아니라 가격 신호의 약점을 제기한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence points out a flaw in the idea that price alone signals quality: anyone can copy a price tag. The next sentence then answers that flaw by explaining that brand reputation makes the signal credible, so C is correct. A is wrong because, although the sentence raises a problem, the text refines the signaling explanation rather than abandoning it. B is wrong because the new firm appears only as a hypothetical copycat, not as an example of pricing helping entry. D is wrong because the sentence doesn't restate the information gap; it challenges whether price can bridge it.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 앞선 가격 신호 설명의 한계를 제기하고, 다음 문장이 브랜드 평판으로 이를 해결하므로 C가 정답임을 직접 확인. A(한계 제기는 맞으나 '폐기'는 과장), B(신생 기업 언급은 있으나 역할 왜곡)는 부분적 근거를 가진 오답이고 D도 주제상 그럴듯함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 창작 경제 설명문으로 저작권 우려 없음. 두 단계 판단(양보 표지 인식 + 후속 문장과의 연결)이 필요해 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 'Yet'으로 약점을 제기한 뒤 이어지는 해결 문장과 연결해야 하는 두 단계 판단 문항임. 오답 B와 D는 지문 요소(신생 기업, 정보 비대칭)를 부분적으로 활용하고 있어 적절함. A는 'abandoned' 때문에 비교적 쉽게 배제됨.

options: , in effect,

in effect,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Urban mail delivery ... generates steady surpluses"와 빈칸 뒤 "those surpluses pay for ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 잇고 전환어구 in effect를 뒤 절 앞에 두려면 세미콜론과 쉼표가 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 전환어구를 쉼표로만 감싸 두 독립절을 이어서 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C의 which는 관계절을 만들지만 뒤에 이미 주어 those surpluses가 있어 문장 구조가 무너진다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("Urban mail delivery ... generates steady surpluses") and the text after it ("those surpluses pay for ...") are both independent clauses, each with its own subject and verb. To join them and put the transition "in effect" at the start of the second clause, you need a semicolon followed by a comma, so B is correct. A sets off the transition with commas only, so it joins two independent clauses with just a comma, which is a comma splice. C uses "which" to start a relative clause, but the words after it already have their own subject ("those surpluses"), so the sentence breaks down. D has no punctuation at all between the clauses, which makes it a run-on sentence.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 주어·동사를 갖춘 독립절("Urban mail delivery ... generates steady surpluses" / "those surpluses pay for ...")임을 직접 확인. B(세미콜론 + 전환어구 + 쉼표)만 올바른 경계. A는 comma splice, D는 run-on, C는 which 뒤에 별도 주어가 와서 구조 붕괴. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조이며 오류 없음. 삽입구("dense and inexpensive ...")가 주절 구조 파악을 다소 어렵게 하고 A·D가 그럴듯한 오답이어서 medium에 적합. 저작권 의심 없음(독창적 지문).

problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "Because employers ... to obtain," is a complete sentence because it contains the main clause "they rely ...," and "the degree sorts candidates ..." after the blank is also an independent clause. That means you need a strong boundary between them. D works because the semicolon separates the two clauses and the comma after "in this view" sets off the introductory phrase of the second clause. A looks right because it puts commas around "in this view," but the two independent clauses are still joined only by commas, which is a comma splice. B and C also connect the clauses with just a comma or with no punctuation at all, so they create a comma splice and a run-on, respectively.

by contrast,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Some variation ... arises ... source"와 빈칸 뒤 "other variation stems ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 이어야 하고, 접속부사 "by contrast"는 뒤에 쉼표를 붙여 다음 절과 구분하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 세미콜론은 맞지만 접속부사 뒤에 필요한 쉼표가 빠졌다. D는 첫 절과 둘째 절 사이에 아무 문장부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("Some variation ... arises ... single source") and the text after it ("other variation stems ...") are both independent clauses. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and the transitional phrase "by contrast" needs a comma after it to set it off from the clause that follows, so A is correct. B links the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C uses the semicolon correctly but leaves out the comma needed after the transitional phrase. D puts no punctuation at all between the two clauses, which makes a run-on sentence.

options: , in contrast,
; in contrast,
, in contrast
in contrast,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'Affiliate marketing reverses ... result'는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 'an affiliate ... earns nothing ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 접속부사 'in contrast'는 두 절을 이어 줄 수 없으므로 앞에 세미콜론이 있어야 하고, 뒤에는 쉼표를 둔다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 접속부사를 쉼표로만 감싸서 쉼표 접합 오류가 생기고, C도 쉼표 접합인 데다 'in contrast' 뒤에 쉼표까지 빠졌다. D는 두 독립절을 아무 문장부호 없이 붙여 쓴 무종지문이다.

A puts commas around the adverb, which still creates a comma splice. C is also a comma splice, and it leaves out the comma after "in contrast." D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all.

Instead, a female enters the nest of a host bumblebee species in spring, after the host queen has already produced her first workers. It was long assumed that the intruder simply overpowers the colony by force, since she has a thicker exoskeleton and a stronger sting than the host. Yet field observations by entomologists show that many invaders spend hours or even days hiding in the nest debris before acting, gradually acquiring the colony's scent. Once chemically disguised, the cuckoo female often kills or subdues the host queen and then lays her own eggs, which the host workers rear as if they were their own sisters. The intruder also suppresses egg laying by the workers, ensuring that the colony's labor goes almost entirely to raising her offspring.

problem.passage:
Tidepool sculpins (Oligocottus maculosus) are small fish that spend low tide confined to rocky pools along the Pacific coast of North America. When researchers move a sculpin to a pool tens of meters away, it often returns to its original pool within a few tides, even across stretches of unfamiliar shoreline. Early investigators assumed the fish relied mainly on vision, memorizing the shapes of nearby rocks. That explanation, however, could not account for later experiments: sculpins whose eyes were covered still homed successfully, while those whose olfactory organs were blocked wandered at random. Further work showed that each pool carries a slightly distinct chemical signature, shaped by its resident algae and invertebrates, and that sculpins can distinguish water from their home pool from water drawn from neighboring pools. The researchers concluded that as the incoming tide connects the pools, the fish follow faint chemical traces back toward familiar water, using visual cues only once they are close.

problem.passage:
The mimic octopus (Thaumoctopus mimicus), found in the shallow, sandy waters of Indonesia, is known for imitating a range of other animals. By flattening its body and arms and swimming close to the seafloor, it can resemble a toxic flatfish; by burying six arms and waving the remaining two in opposite directions, it can look like a venomous sea snake. Early observers assumed the octopus simply shifted among these disguises at random. Researchers who have filmed the animal over many hours, however, report a different pattern: the octopus seems to choose its imitation based on the threat it faces. When damselfish harass it, for example, it often takes on the sea snake form, an animal that hunts damselfish. Because open sand offers few places to hide, this ability to match a disguise to a particular attacker may be what allows the octopus to forage in daylight.

problem.passage:
Mantis shrimp are often described as having the most sophisticated eyes in the animal kingdom: whereas humans rely on three types of color photoreceptors, some mantis shrimp species possess twelve. For years, researchers assumed that this abundance must allow the animals to distinguish between colors with extraordinary precision. However, when biologist Hanne Thoen and colleagues trained mantis shrimp to choose between pairs of closely matched colors, the animals performed worse than many species with far fewer receptor types, often failing to tell apart hues that humans separate easily. The researchers proposed that mantis shrimp do not compare signals across receptors, as human brains do, but instead recognize colors directly by which receptor fires, a system that sacrifices fine discrimination for speed. Notably, the same eyes also detect circularly polarized light, a capacity that appears to serve signaling between individuals rather than precise color judgment.

D can look right because the sentence compares permanent spines with spines grown in response to a cue, but that comparison happens inside the sentence itself; its relationship to the sentence before it is a consequence, not a contrast.

advisory.note: 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 문장의 번식 비용에서 끌어낸 가정적 귀결이므로 Thus가 맞다. B(가상 상황을 예시로 오인할 수 있음)와 D(문장 안의 대비)가 부분적으로 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 해 medium 난이도에 맞다. Daphnia의 카이로몬 유도 방어와 그 비용은 실제 연구 내용과 일치한다.

problem.passage:
Bladderworts are rootless aquatic plants that capture tiny prey with hundreds of hollow underwater bladders. Each bladder slowly pumps water out through its walls, creating low internal pressure, and then waits with its trapdoor sealed shut. When a water flea brushes against trigger hairs near the door, the door buckles inward and water rushes in, carrying the prey with it. Researchers long assumed that the hairs worked like a mechanical lever that pried the door open. __High-speed filming by physicist Olivier Vincent and colleagues, however, showed that a bladder sometimes fires with no contact at all, once its internal pressure drops past a critical point.__ This finding suggests that the door is held near a point of instability, so the trigger hairs merely provide a tiny final push rather than doing the work of opening it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Bladderworts are rootless aquatic plants that capture tiny prey with hundreds of hollow underwater bladders. Each bladder slowly pumps water out through its walls, creating low internal pressure, and then waits with its trapdoor sealed shut. When a water flea brushes against trigger hairs near the door, the door buckles inward and water rushes in, carrying the prey with it. Researchers long assumed that the hairs worked like a mechanical lever that pried the door open. __High-speed filming by physicist Olivier Vincent and colleagues, however, showed that a bladder sometimes fires with no contact at all, once its internal pressure drops past a critical point.__ This finding suggests that the door is held near a point of instability, so the trigger hairs merely provide a tiny final push rather than doing the work of opening it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the process by which a bladder lowers its internal pressure before any prey comes near.
It presents evidence that trigger hairs play no role at all in the way bladderworts capture prey.
It explains why researchers first believed that the trigger hairs acted as a mechanical lever.
It reports an observation that challenges an earlier assumption and sets up a revised interpretation.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 접촉 없이도 덫이 작동한다는 촬영 결과를 보고하여, 털이 지렛대 역할을 한다는 기존 가정에 의문을 제기하고, 마지막 문장의 수정된 해석(문이 불안정점 근처에 있고 털은 마지막 작은 자극만 준다)을 이끈다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 압력이 언급되긴 하지만 압력을 낮추는 과정은 앞 문장에서 설명되며, 밑줄 문장의 역할은 아니다. B는 지나치다. 지문은 털이 '작은 마지막 자극'을 준다고 하므로 역할이 전혀 없다는 뜻이 아니다. C는 기존 가정을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 가정이 생긴 이유를 설명하는 것이 아니라 반박한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence reports filming that showed bladders can fire without any contact. This calls into question the old belief that the hairs work as a lever, and it leads into the final sentence's new interpretation: the door sits near instability, and the hairs only give a small final push. That makes D correct. A mentions pressure, but the earlier sentence is the one that describes how the pressure gets lowered, so that isn't the underlined sentence's role. B goes too far, because the text says the hairs still supply a tiny push, so they do play some role. C mentions the earlier belief, but the underlined sentence challenges that belief instead of explaining why people held it.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 기존 가정(지렛대)을 뒤집는 촬영 증거를 제시하고 마지막 문장의 수정 해석을 이끌므로 D가 정확함. A는 압력 저하 과정(앞 문장 내용), C는 가정의 '이유' 설명이라는 점에서 부분적 근거만 있어 비교가 필요하고, B는 '전혀 역할 없음'으로 과장되어 배제됨. Vincent 등(2011)의 고속 촬영 및 자발적 발화 관찰은 실제 연구 결과와 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 두 단계 판단(기존 가정 파악 + 밑줄 문장의 전환 역할 확인)이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Vincent 등(2011)의 자발적 발사 연구 내용과 맞는다. B는 '접촉 없이 발사'를 근거로 삼아 그럴듯하고, A와 C도 지문 요소를 빌려 와 중간 난이도에 맞다. D는 'however'가 신호어 역할을 해 다소 쉬운 편이지만 허용 범위다.

problem.passage:
Many plants trade carbon with soil fungi called arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi: the plant supplies sugars and lipids from photosynthesis, and the fungus delivers phosphorus gathered by its threadlike hyphae. Researchers have often described this exchange as a stable partnership in which both sides simply benefit. Work led by ecologist Toby Kiers complicates that picture. When Kiers's team gave roots access to several fungal strains, some of which hoarded phosphorus rather than passing it on, the roots sent more carbon to the strains that delivered more phosphorus. __The fungi, in turn, moved more phosphorus to roots that supplied more carbon, even shifting nutrients through their networks toward parts of the soil where phosphorus was scarce and could therefore fetch a better "price."__ Taken together, these findings suggest that the symbiosis is better understood as a market in which each partner rewards the other in proportion to what it receives.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Many plants trade carbon with soil fungi called arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi: the plant supplies sugars and lipids from photosynthesis, and the fungus delivers phosphorus gathered by its threadlike hyphae. Researchers have often described this exchange as a stable partnership in which both sides simply benefit. Work led by ecologist Toby Kiers complicates that picture. When Kiers's team gave roots access to several fungal strains, some of which hoarded phosphorus rather than passing it on, the roots sent more carbon to the strains that delivered more phosphorus. __The fungi, in turn, moved more phosphorus to roots that supplied more carbon, even shifting nutrients through their networks toward parts of the soil where phosphorus was scarce and could therefore fetch a better "price."__ Taken together, these findings suggest that the symbiosis is better understood as a market in which each partner rewards the other in proportion to what it receives.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence that the fungi benefit from the exchange more than the host plants do, which weakens the view that the relationship is a partnership.
It shows that the behavior seen in the plants is also found in the fungi, which supports the conclusion stated in the final sentence.
It explains how the uncooperative strains managed to obtain carbon from roots, which accounts for the hoarding described earlier.
It describes a finding that conflicts with the root experiment, which makes the conclusion in the final sentence less certain.
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 식물이 인을 더 많이 주는 균주에게 탄소를 더 보낸다는 결과이고, 밑줄 문장은 균류도 탄소를 더 주는 뿌리에게 인을 더 보낸다는 결과를 보여 준다. 이렇게 양쪽 모두 보상한다는 점이 마지막 문장의 '시장' 결론을 뒷받침하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 균류가 더 많은 이익을 얻는다고 하지만, 지문은 어느 쪽이 더 이익을 보는지 비교하지 않는다. C는 비협조적 균주의 행동을 설명한다고 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그런 균주가 탄소를 얻는 방법을 다루지 않는다. D는 앞 실험과 충돌한다고 하지만, 밑줄 문장은 앞 실험과 같은 방향의 결과로 결론을 강화한다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before it shows that roots send more carbon to fungal strains that deliver more phosphorus. The underlined sentence shows the same pattern from the fungi's side: they send more phosphorus to roots that supply more carbon. Because both partners reward each other, this supports the "market" conclusion in the final sentence, so B is correct. A is wrong because the text never compares which partner benefits more. C is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain how hoarding strains get carbon. D is wrong because the finding agrees with the root experiment and makes the conclusion stronger, not weaker.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 앞 문장(뿌리가 인을 더 주는 균주에 탄소를 더 보냄)의 거울상 결과(균류도 탄소를 더 주는 뿌리에 인을 더 보냄)로, "in turn"과 "Taken together"가 이를 마지막 문장의 '시장' 결론과 연결한다. B 정답 확인. A는 지문이 이익의 크기를 비교하지 않으므로 오답, C는 비협조 균주의 탄소 획득 방법을 다루지 않으므로 오답, D는 결과가 앞 실험과 같은 방향이므로 오답. 해설(한/영) 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 내용은 Kiers 등(2011)의 상호 보상 실험 및 Whiteside 등(2019)의 인 희소 지역으로의 이동 연구와 부합하며 원문 복제 흔적 없음. 정답 도출에 앞 문장 + 마지막 문장 두 정보를 연결해야 하고, A·D는 '파트너십 재검토'라는 지문 흐름에 부분적으로 기대어 비교가 필요하므로 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: Kiers et al. 2011 Science 및 2019 연구의 실제 내용과 맞음. 오답 A, D는 '파트너십 관점을 복잡하게 한다'는 문맥 때문에 그럴듯하게 보이며, 두 단계의 구조 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
For decades, biologists assumed that every food web on Earth ultimately depended on sunlight captured by photosynthesis. The 1977 discovery of dense communities of tubeworms, clams, and shrimp clustered around hydrothermal vents on the Galápagos Rift challenged that view. Researchers soon found that the base of these communities consists of chemosynthetic bacteria, which oxidize hydrogen sulfide escaping from the vents and use the released energy to convert carbon dioxide into organic compounds. __Yet the oxygen these bacteria need to oxidize sulfide is itself a by-product of photosynthesis at the ocean's surface, carried to the depths by circulating seawater.__ Vent ecosystems, then, are better described not as fully independent of the Sun but as powered by a different chemical route that still relies, indirectly, on sunlit waters far above.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: For decades, biologists assumed that every food web on Earth ultimately depended on sunlight captured by photosynthesis. The 1977 discovery of dense communities of tubeworms, clams, and shrimp clustered around hydrothermal vents on the Galápagos Rift challenged that view. Researchers soon found that the base of these communities consists of chemosynthetic bacteria, which oxidize hydrogen sulfide escaping from the vents and use the released energy to convert carbon dioxide into organic compounds. __Yet the oxygen these bacteria need to oxidize sulfide is itself a by-product of photosynthesis at the ocean's surface, carried to the depths by circulating seawater.__ Vent ecosystems, then, are better described not as fully independent of the Sun but as powered by a different chemical route that still relies, indirectly, on sunlit waters far above.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains the chemical process by which vent bacteria convert hydrogen sulfide into organic compounds.
It presents evidence that overturns the 1977 finding that vent communities rely on chemosynthetic bacteria.
It introduces a qualification that limits how far the vent discovery departs from the earlier assumption about sunlight.
It describes a factor that explains why vent communities are densely clustered rather than widely dispersed.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 시작해 박테리아에 필요한 산소가 결국 표층 광합성에서 온다고 지적하며, 열수구 생태계가 태양과 완전히 무관하다는 해석을 제한한다. 마지막 문장이 이를 '간접적으로 의존한다'고 정리하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 산화 과정 자체가 앞 문장에서 이미 설명되었고 밑줄 문장은 산소의 출처를 말할 뿐이다. B는 박테리아가 기반이라는 발견을 뒤집는 것이 아니라 그 의미를 한정하는 것이므로 틀리다. D는 군집이 밀집한 이유는 지문에서 다뤄지지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet" and points out that the oxygen the bacteria use comes from surface photosynthesis, which limits the claim that vent ecosystems are totally independent of the Sun. The final sentence confirms this by calling the reliance "indirect," so C is correct. A is wrong because the previous sentence already describes the oxidation process; the underlined sentence only identifies where the oxygen comes from. B is wrong because the sentence doesn't reject the finding that bacteria form the base of the food web; it narrows what that finding means. D is wrong because the text never explains why the communities cluster densely.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'Yet'으로 전환하여 열수구 박테리아의 산소가 표층 광합성에서 온다는 점을 들어 '태양과 무관'이라는 해석을 제한하고, 마지막 문장이 '간접적 의존'으로 이를 정리하므로 C가 정답임을 직접 확인함. A는 산화 언급으로, B는 'Yet'의 대조 신호로 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하고 D도 표면적으로 그럴듯하여 medium 기준에 부합. 1977년 갈라파고스 열곡 발견, 황화수소 산화 화학합성, 산소의 광합성 기원 등 과학적 사실 정확. 한·영 해설 결론과 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 창작 설명문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 'Yet' 다음의 단서와 마지막 문장의 결론을 이어 읽어야 해서 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A(앞 문장 내용과 일부 겹침)와 B('Yet'이 주는 반박 느낌)는 그럴듯한 오답이다. D는 비교적 약하지만 말은 된다. 사실관계(1977년 갈라파고스 열곡, 황화수소 산화 시 광합성에서 온 O2 사용)는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
The floating leaves of the giant water lily Victoria amazonica can grow wider than two meters, yet each one supports its own weight on the water's surface without sinking or tearing. Botanists long assumed that the leaf's size was possible simply because water carries most of the load. __Studies of the leaf's underside, however, revealed a dense lattice of thick, air-filled ribs radiating from the center and linked by cross-veins, a pattern that spreads weight across the whole surface much as girders do in a bridge deck.__ Because the trapped air also adds buoyancy, the ribs let the plant build a huge leaf from a remarkably thin and light sheet of tissue, an efficiency that reportedly inspired the iron framework of a nineteenth-century glasshouse.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: The floating leaves of the giant water lily Victoria amazonica can grow wider than two meters, yet each one supports its own weight on the water's surface without sinking or tearing. Botanists long assumed that the leaf's size was possible simply because water carries most of the load. __Studies of the leaf's underside, however, revealed a dense lattice of thick, air-filled ribs radiating from the center and linked by cross-veins, a pattern that spreads weight across the whole surface much as girders do in a bridge deck.__ Because the trapped air also adds buoyancy, the ribs let the plant build a huge leaf from a remarkably thin and light sheet of tissue, an efficiency that reportedly inspired the iron framework of a nineteenth-century glasshouse.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives evidence that supports the botanists' assumption that water alone carries the weight of the leaf.
It describes an engineering design that the text later shows was copied from the leaf.
It points out a weakness in the leaf's structure that limits how large the leaf can become.
It brings up a structural feature that complicates an earlier explanation and is then explored further.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작해, 물이 무게를 대부분 떠받친다는 기존 가정만으로는 설명이 부족함을 보여 주는 잎맥 격자 구조를 소개하고, 다음 문장이 그 구조의 부력과 효율을 더 설명하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 이 문장이 가정을 뒷받침한다고 하지만 실제로는 가정을 보완·수정한다. B는 다리 비유와 온실 언급에 끌린 오답으로, 밑줄 문장이 묘사하는 것은 공학 설계가 아니라 잎의 구조이며 모방된 쪽은 온실이다. C는 구조를 약점으로 보지만 지문은 이 구조를 큰 잎을 가능하게 하는 강점으로 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence opens with "however" and introduces the rib lattice, which shows that the botanists' assumption that water does most of the work is incomplete; the next sentence then explains how the ribs add buoyancy and efficiency, so D is correct. A is wrong because the sentence revises the assumption instead of supporting it. B is tempting because of the bridge comparison and the glasshouse mention, but the sentence describes the leaf's structure, not an engineering design, and it was the glasshouse that copied the leaf. C is wrong because the text presents the ribs as a strength that makes a huge leaf possible, not a weakness.

problem.passage:
Zebra mussels spread through North American waterways largely because of their microscopic larvae. These free-swimming veligers, which drift in the current for several weeks before settling, are easily drawn into the intake pipes of power plants and water treatment facilities. Once inside, the larvae attach to any hard ______ within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow a pipe's opening enough to sharply reduce the flow of water.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Zebra mussels spread through North American waterways largely because of their microscopic larvae. These free-swimming veligers, which drift in the current for several weeks before settling, are easily drawn into the intake pipes of power plants and water treatment facilities. Once inside, the larvae attach to any hard ______ within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow a pipe's opening enough to sharply reduce the flow of water.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: surface, and grow rapidly,
surface and grow rapidly;
surface, and grow rapidly
surface and grow rapidly,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "the larvae attach ... and grow rapidly"는 완전한 독립절이고, 뒤의 "within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow..."도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결해야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A와 D는 독립절 두 개를 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. C는 두 절 사이에 아무 부호도 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 되고, 하나의 주어가 갖는 복합 동사 "attach ... and grow" 사이에 불필요한 쉼표까지 들어가 있다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "the larvae attach to any hard surface and grow rapidly," form a complete independent clause, and "within a few years, the accumulated shells can narrow..." is a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so B is correct. A and D link the two clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between the clauses, which creates a run-on sentence, and it also adds an unneeded comma inside the compound verb "attach ... and grow."

problem.passage:
In a clownfish colony, all of whose members shelter among the stinging tentacles of a single sea anemone, only two fish breed: the largest individual, which is always female, mates with the second-largest fish, the colony's sole breeding male______ when the female dies, this male changes sex within weeks, and the next-largest fish in the colony grows rapidly to become the new breeding male.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In a clownfish colony, all of whose members shelter among the stinging tentacles of a single sea anemone, only two fish breed: the largest individual, which is always female, mates with the second-largest fish, the colony's sole breeding male______ when the female dies, this male changes sex within weeks, and the next-largest fish in the colony grows rapidly to become the new breeding male.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: — and
and
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 동격어구 "the colony's sole breeding male"로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "when the female dies, this male changes sex..."도 독립절이므로 두 절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 C가 정답이다. A는 동격어구를 쉼표로 닫는 점은 맞지만 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 접속사 and를 넣어 절 연결은 해결하지만, 쉼표로 시작한 동격어구를 대시로 닫아 부호 짝이 맞지 않는다. D는 쉼표 없이 and만 써서 쉼표로 열린 동격어구가 닫히지 않으므로 "male and when..."이 하나로 읽힌다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank is an independent clause ending with the appositive "the colony's sole breeding male," and the text after it ("when the female dies, this male changes sex...") is also an independent clause, so a semicolon correctly joins them, which makes C the answer. A properly closes the appositive with a comma, but a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so it creates a comma splice. B adds "and" to link the clauses, but the appositive opens with a comma and can't be closed with a dash, so the punctuation doesn't match. D uses "and" with no comma, which leaves the appositive opened by a comma unclosed, so "male and when..." runs together.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞(콜론 뒤 독립절, 동격어구로 종결)과 뒤(종속절+주절 독립절)를 세미콜론으로 잇는 C가 유일하게 표준 규범에 맞음. A는 comma splice, B의 "— and"는 쉼표로 연 동격어구를 대시로 닫는 비표준 조합, D는 쉼표 없는 and로 동격어구가 닫히지 않고 긴 독립절 연결에 부적절. 해설 한·영 일치, 선택지 글자 참조 정확. 흰동가리 성전환(암컷 사망 시 수컷→암컷, 차순위 개체가 번식 수컷으로 성장) 사실 정확. 동격어구 인식 + 절 구조 판단의 2단계로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 콜론 뒤 절 안에 동격어구가 있고 그 뒤를 세미콜론으로 끊는 구조다. 쉼표 오용(A)과 부호 짝 불일치(B)를 함께 판단해야 하므로 medium 난이도에 적합하다.

options: males; these
males, these
males these

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "females consistently paired with the reddest available males"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "these redder males ... brought more food"도 삽입구 "it turned out"을 포함한 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 되고, C는 아무 부호 없이 이어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 옳지만 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표가 들어가 표준 문장부호 규칙에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "females consistently paired with the reddest available males," form an independent clause. The words after the blank, "these redder males ... brought more food," form another independent clause, even with the interrupting phrase "it turned out." A semicolon can correctly join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice, and C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D is right to use the coordinating conjunction "and," but the extra comma after "and" doesn't follow standard punctuation rules.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이며("found that females ... males" / "these redder males, it turned out, also brought..."), 세미콜론 연결(A)만 표준 규칙에 맞음. B는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 and 뒤 불필요한 쉼표로 오답. 삽입구 "it turned out"이 절 구조 파악을 요구하고 D가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. Geoffrey Hill의 house finch 연구는 실제 사실과 부합.

advisory.note: 삽입구 'it turned out'이 두 번째 절을 끊어 놓아 독립절인지 판단하는 데 한 단계가 더 필요하므로 medium에 맞음. D는 명백히 틀린 오답이라 약하지만, B·C는 훑어 읽으면 고를 만함. Hill의 Michigan house finch 연구 내용과도 일치함.
