Once inside an elm's water-conducting xylem, the fungus spreads rapidly, and the tree responds by plugging its own vessels with gummy deposits and balloon-like growths called tyloses. This defense, intended to wall off the invader, backfires ______ water can no longer rise to the crown, so leaves wilt, yellow, and drop, often within a single summer.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: badly, with the blocked vessels,
badly: with the vessels blocked,
badly, the vessels being blocked,
badly; with the vessels blocked
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This defense ... backfires badly"는 독립절이고, 그 뒤 "water can no longer rise..."도 주어와 동사를 가진 독립절이며, 앞 절을 설명한다. B는 콜론으로 두 절을 연결하고, 도입 전치사구 뒤에 쉼표를 찍으므로 맞다. problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank, "This defense ... backfires badly," form an independent clause, and "water can no longer rise..." is also an independent clause that explains the first one. B joins them with a colon and puts a comma after the introductory phrase, so it's correct. A and C use only a comma to join two independent clauses, which creates a comma splice. In D, the semicolon would work, but there's no comma between the introductory phrase "with the vessels blocked" and the main clause "water can...," and that comma is needed.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: The Namib desert beetle Stenocara gracilipes survives in one of Earth's driest places by collecting water from fog. Its wing covers are dotted with tiny water-attracting bumps set among water-repelling waxy grooves, a surface pattern that directs moisture with remarkable precision ______ droplets condense on the bumps, grow heavy, and then roll along the grooves toward the beetle's mouth.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: , droplets
droplets
: droplets
, which droplets
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 동격구(a surface pattern ... precision)로 끝나는 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 droplets condense ... 도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며 앞 내용을 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 동격구 앞의 쉼표와 짝을 이루는 것처럼 보이지만, 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 오류(comma splice)이다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. D의 which는 관계절을 만들려 하지만 droplets가 주어 자리를 차지해 which가 절 안에서 맡을 역할이 없으므로 비문이다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank is a complete independent clause that ends with an appositive ("a surface pattern ... precision"). The part after the blank, "droplets condense ... mouth," is also an independent clause, and it explains how that pattern directs moisture. A colon is the right way to introduce that kind of explanation, so C is correct. A might look right because it seems to pair with the comma before the appositive, but a comma alone can't join two independent clauses, so it creates a comma splice. B joins the two clauses with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D starts what looks like a relative clause, but "droplets" already fills the subject slot, so "which" has no job in the clause and the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

A는 comma splice, B는 run-on, D는 which 뒤에 주어 droplets가 와서 비문. 과학 사실(Stenocara gracilipes의 친수성 돌기·소수성 홈 구조)도 정확. 동격구 뒤에 빈칸이 와 앞부분의 절 경계를 파악해야 하므로 medium에 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 정답·오답 근거가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 동격구 뒤 독립절 연결을 묻는다. 동격구의 쉼표가 A를 그럴듯하게 만들고, D는 관계절 함정이다. 사실관계(나미브 사막 딱정벌레가 친수성 돌기로 안개 수분을 모으는 것)는 통상 설명과 일치한다.

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how different in appearance the two generations of a fern are. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The sporophyte is a leafy plant that may exceed a meter in height, whereas the gametophyte is a flat, heart-shaped structure typically under a centimeter wide.
The sporophyte produces spores on its fronds, whereas the gametophyte produces eggs and sperm that need a film of water for fertilization.
The sporophyte begins life drawing nourishment from the gametophyte, whereas the gametophyte itself develops from a germinating spore.
The sporophyte and the gametophyte are both free-living generations, and each one gives rise to the other in the fern's life cycle.
problem.explanation: 목표는 두 세대의 '외형(모양·크기)' 차이를 강조하는 것이다. A는 1미터가 넘는 잎이 무성한 포자체와 1센티미터도 안 되는 납작한 하트 모양 배우체를 대비해 형태 차이를 직접 보여 준다. B는 두 세대를 대조하지만 생식 기능(포자 대 난자·정자)의 차이일 뿐 외형 차이가 아니다. C는 영양 관계와 발생 순서를 설명할 뿐 생김새는 다루지 않는다. D는 두 세대의 공통점과 순환 관계를 말하므로 차이를 강조하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to emphasize how the two generations differ in appearance, meaning their shape and size. A does this directly by contrasting a leafy sporophyte that can grow over a meter tall with a flat, heart-shaped gametophyte less than a centimeter wide. B does contrast the two generations, but by their reproductive roles (spores versus eggs and sperm), not by how they look. C describes how the generations are nourished and develop, but it says nothing about their appearance. D points out what the two generations have in common and how they cycle, so it doesn't highlight any difference.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 목표가 '외형(appearance)' 차이 강조이며 A만 크기·형태(1m 이상 잎 무성한 식물 vs 1cm 미만 납작한 하트 모양)를 직접 대비함. B·C는 'whereas' 대조 구조로 노트 정보를 정확히 사용해 훑어 읽으면 매력적이나 생식 기능·영양/발생 관계로 외형이 아님. problem.passage:
Auroras are usually confined to a ring-shaped zone around each magnetic pole, called the auroral oval, where charged particles guided by Earth's magnetic field strike the upper atmosphere. During a geomagnetic storm, however, this zone can shift dramatically. When a dense, fast-moving burst of solar wind arrives, it presses against the magnetosphere, the magnetic bubble surrounding Earth, squeezing its sunward side closer to the planet. If the magnetic field carried by the solar wind points southward, opposite to Earth's own field at that boundary, the two fields can link up, allowing far more energy to pour into the magnetosphere than usual. As this energy is stored and then released on the planet's night side, the auroral oval widens and pushes toward the equator. That is why, during the strongest storms, observers in places such as southern Europe or the central United States, far from the polar regions where auroras normally appear, can occasionally see the sky glow red and green.

Based on the text, why are auroras sometimes visible at latitudes well outside the polar regions?

problem.question: Based on the text, why are auroras sometimes visible at latitudes well outside the polar regions?
options: Dense solar wind pushes the magnetosphere's sunward side closer to Earth, which moves auroral displays from the night side to the day side.
Energy entering the magnetosphere when the solar wind's field opposes Earth's field causes the auroral oval to expand toward the equator.
Charged particles from the solar wind bypass Earth's magnetic field entirely during storms and strike the atmosphere at lower latitudes.
The auroral oval normally shifts toward the equator whenever the solar wind's magnetic field points in the same direction as Earth's field.
problem.explanation: 지문은 태양풍 자기장이 남향, 즉 지구 자기장과 반대일 때 두 자기장이 연결되어 에너지가 대량 유입되고, 이것이 밤쪽에서 방출되며 오로라 오벌이 넓어져 적도 쪽으로 이동한다고 설명하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 자기권 압축이라는 실제 언급된 사실을 사용하지만, 오로라가 낮쪽으로 옮겨간다는 내용은 지문에 없고 에너지 방출은 밤쪽에서 일어난다. C는 입자가 자기장의 안내를 받는다는 지문 내용과 반대로 자기장을 '완전히 우회한다'고 말한다. D는 방향 조건을 뒤집었고, 오벌 확장이 '평상시' 일어나는 일이라고 잘못 서술한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text explains that when the solar wind's magnetic field points southward, opposite to Earth's field, the two fields link up and far more energy flows into the magnetosphere; when that energy is released on the night side, the auroral oval widens toward the equator. That makes B correct. A starts from a real detail (the magnetosphere gets compressed), but the text never says auroras move to the day side, and it says the energy is released on the night side. C contradicts the text, which says particles are guided by Earth's magnetic field, not that they bypass it. D reverses the direction condition and wrongly presents the expansion as something that happens normally.

problem.passage:
In the 1920s, Serbian engineer Milutin Milankovitch calculated how slow changes in Earth's orbit alter the sunlight reaching high northern latitudes in summer. Three cycles are involved: the orbit's shape (eccentricity) shifts over roughly 100,000 years, the tilt of Earth's axis varies over about 41,000 years, and the direction the axis points (precession) wobbles over about 23,000 years. None of these cycles changes the planet's total yearly sunlight by more than a fraction of a percent. Yet sediment cores show that ice ages have come and gone in step with them.

Researchers now explain this mismatch through feedbacks within the climate system. When northern summers grow slightly cooler, some snow survives the season, and the brighter surface reflects more sunlight, cooling the region further. Colder oceans also absorb more carbon dioxide, weakening the greenhouse effect worldwide. In this view, orbital cycles act less as the engine of glacial change than as a pacemaker that sets its timing, while Earth's own processes supply most of the temperature swing.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

C captures both parts. A names the three cycles, but the text says their sunlight effect is tiny, so they cannot act alone. B mentions eccentricity and sediment cores, but the text never ranks the cycles against each other. D brings up carbon feedback but reverses the roles, because the text says the orbit, not carbon dioxide, sets the timing.

On some winter nights in mountain basins such as Utah's Salt Lake Valley, however, the ground loses heat quickly, chilling the air just above it while a layer of warmer air settles overhead like a lid. ______ the surface air, now denser than the layer capping it, stays put, and pollutants released near the ground can accumulate for days until a storm system mixes the layers.

problem.passage:
Many people assume that clear skies simply reflect the absence of weather, but meteorologists view them as the product of an active process. In a high-pressure system, air in the upper atmosphere converges and sinks toward the surface, spiraling outward in a clockwise pattern in the Northern Hemisphere. __As this air descends, it is compressed and warms, which lowers its relative humidity and prevents the water vapor it carries from condensing into clouds.__ This mechanism helps explain why the subtropical belts near 30 degrees north and south latitude, where sinking air from the Hadley circulation persistently accumulates, host many of the world's great deserts, including the Sahara and the Kalahari.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

problem.passage:
Between the 1960s and the late 1980s, the open water of Lake Chad shrank from roughly 25,000 square kilometers to a small fraction of that size, and the lake became a widely cited symbol of environmental collapse. Many early accounts blamed large irrigation projects, which diverted water from the Chari and Logone Rivers, the lake's main sources of water. Hydrologist Jacques Lemoalle and colleagues reexamined the record and concluded that irrigation removed only a modest share of the inflow. __Most of the decline, they found, coincided with the severe Sahel droughts of the 1970s and 1980s, when reduced rainfall across the basin cut river discharge far more sharply than any diversion could.__ This finding does not excuse heavy water withdrawals, but it suggests that efforts to restore the lake must account chiefly for the region's highly variable climate.

problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence follows the researchers' conclusion that irrigation took only a modest share of the inflow, and it names drought-driven rainfall loss as the main cause, so it identifies a factor judged more important than the one earlier accounts emphasized (A). B gets the relationship backward: the drought evidence challenges the irrigation explanation instead of supporting it. C contradicts the final sentence, which says restoration must account chiefly for climate, so climate is not excluded. D is wrong because the sentence strengthens the conclusion that irrigation had a modest effect rather than limiting it.

problem.passage:
For decades, astronomers assumed that supernovae, the explosive deaths of massive stars, were the main source of the universe's gold, platinum, and other heavy elements formed through the rapid neutron-capture process, or r-process. In 2017, however, detectors registered gravitational waves from two neutron stars spiraling into each other, and telescopes soon spotted the glowing debris of the collision. The light from that debris carried the spectral signature of freshly made heavy elements in quantities that astonished researchers. __Yet a single well-observed event cannot reveal how often such collisions occurred in the early universe, which is precisely what determines whether they could have supplied most of the heavy elements found in ancient stars.__ For that reason, many astrophysicists now treat neutron star mergers as a confirmed source of r-process elements but not yet as the proven dominant one.

It identifies a limitation of the 2017 observation that tempers the conclusion researchers can draw from it.

A는 초신성이 언급되긴 하지만 밑줄 문장은 초신성이 우세하다는 증거를 제시하지 않는다. C는 많은 양의 중원소가 앞 문장에 나오지만 밑줄 문장은 그 원인을 설명하지 않는다. D는 밑줄 문장이 관측의 출처 자체를 의심하는 것이 아니라 일반화 범위를 제한할 뿐이다.

The next sentence then gives a cautious conclusion: mergers are a confirmed source of these elements but not yet the proven main one. That makes B correct. A is wrong because supernovae do come up in the text, but the underlined sentence gives no evidence that they were the main source. C is wrong because the large quantities of elements are mentioned in the sentence before, but the underlined sentence doesn't explain why there were so many. D is wrong because the sentence doesn't question where the 2017 signal came from. It only limits how far the result can be generalized.

options: orbit are surprisingly crowded:
orbit, are surprisingly crowded,
orbit; are surprisingly crowded:
orbit, are surprisingly crowded:
problem.explanation: "which sit ... orbit"는 비제한적 삽입절이라 앞에 쉼표가 있으므로 뒤에도 쉼표로 닫은 뒤 동사 "are"로 이어가야 한다. 또 "are surprisingly crowded" 뒤에는 독립절이 이어지고, 이 절이 '붐빈다'는 말을 구체적으로 설명하므로 콜론이 알맞다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 삽입절을 닫는 쉼표가 빠졌다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 잇는 쉼표 연결 오류(comma splice)이다. C는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓는다.
problem.explanationEn: The clause "which sit ... orbit" is a nonessential clause that opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "are." After "are surprisingly crowded," a full independent clause follows, and it explains how crowded the regions are, so a colon fits. That makes D correct. A leaves out the comma that closes the nonessential clause. B joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb.

options: flip may have taken only a few thousand years, whereas

problem.explanation: "whereas"는 종속접속사이므로 "whereas the polarity bands ... span ..."는 종속절이며, 앞의 주절에 쉼표로 연결하는 것이 맞다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 독립절이 와야 하는데 whereas 절은 종속절이라 틀리다. C는 종속접속사와 그 절의 주어 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣었다. D는 "Whereas ..."를 문장으로 분리해 주절 없는 문장 조각을 만든다.
problem.explanationEn: "Whereas" is a subordinating conjunction, so "whereas the polarity bands ... span ..." is a dependent clause, and it should attach to the main clause with a comma. That makes A correct. B is wrong because a semicolon needs an independent clause after it, and a whereas clause is dependent. C puts an unneeded comma between the conjunction and the subject of its clause. D breaks off "Whereas ..." as its own sentence, which leaves a fragment with no main clause.

B(세미콜론+종속절), D(조각문)는 whereas를 등위접속사/접속부사처럼 오해하면 고르기 쉬운 매력적 오답이고, C는 접속사 뒤 쉼표 오류로 말이 되는 오답. 사실 관계(Matuyama–Brunhes 약 78만 년 전, 1950~60년대 해양 자기 줄무늬 발견, 반전 소요 수천 년)도 문제없음. 한·영 해설 모두 A 지지, 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Some physicists have proposed ... quantum vacuum"과 뒤 "others explain it ..."는 각각 완전한 독립절이므로, 두 절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 접속사 and 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 and와 others 사이를 잘못 끊는다.

A is a finite verb, but it's plural, so it wrongly agrees with the nearby "impurities" or "boundaries." C and D are participle forms, which can't act as the main verb, so they would leave the sentence incomplete.

problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 "A tiny surface crack"이고, which 관계절은 삽입된 수식어일 뿐이므로 빈칸에는 단수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 와야 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. B는 바로 앞 복수 명사 temperatures에 끌려 고른 복수형이라서 단수 주어 crack과 수가 맞지 않는다. A의 분사형과 D의 to부정사는 정동사가 아니어서 문장에 본동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is "A tiny surface crack." The "which" clause is just an interrupting modifier, so the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a singular subject. That makes C the answer. B is a plural form, and it seems right only if you match it to the nearby plural noun "temperatures," but it doesn't agree with "crack." A (a participle) and D (an infinitive) aren't finite verbs, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb.

problem.passage:
When biomass such as wood chips is heated without oxygen, it undergoes pyrolysis, breaking down into a mix of vapors, gases, and solid char. For decades, engineers assumed that the proportion of liquid bio-oil a reactor produced depended mainly on the final temperature the biomass reached. Chemical engineer Priya Venkataraman and her colleagues tested this assumption by heating identical samples of pine sawdust to the same peak temperature of 500°C while varying how quickly they got there.

Samples heated in under two seconds yielded nearly twice as much condensable vapor as samples heated over several minutes, which instead left behind far more char. The researchers explain that slow heating gives early-forming vapors time to linger inside the particles and react again, recombining into solid residue. Rapid heating, by contrast, drives the vapors out before those secondary reactions can occur. Venkataraman's team concludes that reactor designers aiming for liquid fuels should prioritize the speed of heat transfer, not merely the target temperature.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 최고 온도를 500°C로 똑같이 맞추고 가열 속도만 바꿨더니 빠른 가열에서 응축성 증기가 거의 두 배 나왔다. 그래서 연구진은 목표 온도보다 열전달 속도를 중시해야 한다고 결론 내리며, A가 이를 정확히 요약한다. B는 지문이 의문을 제기한 기존 가정(최종 온도가 핵심)을 그대로 되풀이한다. C는 차(char) 생성을 언급하지만, 차는 느린 가열의 부산물일 뿐 연료 가치를 판단하는 기준이 아니다. D의 무산소 조건은 열분해의 전제 조건으로만 나오며 연구의 변수가 아니었다.
problem.explanationEn: The researchers kept the peak temperature at 500°C for every sample and changed only how fast the samples were heated. The rapidly heated samples gave off nearly twice as much condensable vapor. From this, the team concludes that designers should focus on how fast heat is transferred, not just on the target temperature, and A captures that idea. B repeats the old assumption that the text calls into question. C mentions char, but char is only a by-product of slow heating, not the test for whether the sawdust makes a useful fuel. D points to the lack of oxygen, which is simply part of the definition of pyrolysis, not something the study changed.

problem.passage:
When two dissimilar metals are joined by brazing, atoms from each side gradually migrate across the interface at elevated service temperatures. Engineers long assumed that this interdiffusion was harmless, since it seemed only to blur the boundary between the metals. __In 1947, however, Ernest Kirkendall showed that copper and zinc atoms in brass diffuse at unequal rates, so that more atoms leave one side than arrive to replace them.__ The resulting surplus of vacancies on the faster-diffusing side can cluster into microscopic pores, now called Kirkendall voids. In brazed joints between copper and aluminum, for instance, such voids can accumulate along the interface over years of thermal cycling, weakening the joint until it cracks under loads it once withstood easily.

C goes too far: brass is just the system Kirkendall studied, and the text never ranks it as the most vulnerable alloy. D gets the timing wrong, since the text says copper-aluminum joints crack after years of thermal cycling, not right after they are brazed.

problem.passage:
When a kiln is heated or cooled too quickly, the refractory bricks lining its walls can crack even though they are designed to withstand temperatures above 1,500°C. The problem is not the heat itself but how unevenly it spreads: the brick's surface expands or contracts faster than its interior, and the resulting stress mismatch pulls the material apart. Many engineers have therefore assumed that the most heat-resistant bricks, those with the highest melting points, should also be the least likely to fail during rapid temperature swings. __Yet in trials comparing several brick formulations, materials scientist Lena Oduya found that some dense, high-melting-point bricks fractured sooner than more porous bricks with lower melting points.__ Oduya proposes that the tiny pores act as barriers that stop cracks from spreading, suggesting that a brick's internal structure may matter more than its melting point in resisting thermal shock.

A joins the two clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, so it is a run-on. D puts the semicolon in the wrong place, which attaches "as a result" to the first clause and wrongly presents the shorter processing time as the result instead of the retained fine grains.

The clause after the blank, "when a voltage is applied...," modifies a new main clause, "the mobile outer part... migrates." That means the two independent clauses have to be separated, and a period does that, so A is correct. B makes it look like the "when" clause modifies "flow," but read that way, the next main clause is joined with only a comma, which is a comma splice. D joins the two independent clauses with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on sentence. C puts a semicolon together with the conjunction "and," and that pairing isn't the standard way to join these clauses.

Engineers who protect buildings from earthquakes have long relied on passive dampers, devices filled with oil that resist motion by a fixed amount. Because their resistance cannot change, such dampers are tuned for an expected range of shaking and may perform poorly when an actual earthquake is stronger or weaker than predicted. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers address this limitation. They contain a fluid packed with tiny iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is energized, the particles align into chains along the magnetic field, and within milliseconds the fluid thickens dramatically. By adjusting the current sent to the coil, a building's control system can make the damper stiffer or softer moment by moment as sensors detect changes in ground motion. Notably, MR dampers need only about as much power as a small light bulb to operate, so they can run on backup batteries if an earthquake cuts off a building's main electricity.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "A folded antenna boom ... for launch"와 뒤 "once heated ..., the boom's polymer chains rearrange..."는 각각 독립절이다. "then"은 등위접속사가 아닌 부사이므로 두 절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 필요하고, 그 뒤에 쉼표로 "then"을 구분하는 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다(D는 'then' 뒤 쉼표도 없음). B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("A folded antenna boom ... for launch") and the text after it ("once heated ..., the boom's polymer chains rearrange...") are both independent clauses. Since "then" is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, you need a semicolon to join the two clauses, with a comma after "then," which is why C is correct. A and D connect two independent clauses with only a comma, so they're comma splices (D also leaves out the comma after "then"). B joins the clauses with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Shape-memory polymer cross-linked network recovery and thermal-triggered molecular chain rearrangement in self-deployable aerospace structures

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "A folded antenna boom ... can be stowed compactly for launch"는 독립절, 빈칸 뒤 "once heated ..., the boom's polymer chains rearrange, and the structure springs back ..."도 독립절. "then"은 접속부사이므로 세미콜론 필요 → C(; then,)만 올바름. A(, then,)와 D(, then)는 comma splice, B(then)는 run-on. 지정 정답 C 확인. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 C를 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 자연스러운 영어, 한글 없음. 형상기억고분자의 자가전개 우주구조물 활용은 사실에 부합. 난이도: 두 절의 독립성 판단 + 'then'의 품사 판단이라는 두 단계 추론, 첫 절이 길고 둘째 절이 종속절로 시작해 훑어 읽으면 혼동 가능. A·D는 쉼표 사용으로 부분적 그럴듯함, B도 문장이 읽히기는 함 → medium 적합. 사소: 선택지 B 앞에 공백 두 칸(채점에 영향 없음).

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절이고 'then'은 접속부사이므로 세미콜론을 쓴 C가 유일하게 맞다. 'once heated...'라는 도입 수식어 때문에 뒷절이 독립절인지 바로 보이지 않아, 훑어 읽으면 A나 D를 고르게 되므로 medium 난이도에 맞다. 형식상 사소한 점으로, 선택지 B 앞에 공백이 두 칸 들어가 있다.
